column5: I keep worrying about money and what will happen tomorrow. What did Wesley say about anxiety and taking thought for the future?
column7: #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9
column8:
#29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9, wesley-029-c0003: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. "«Take therefore no thought for the morrow: For the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.»'" Matt. 6:24-34. 1. It is recorded of the nations whom the King of Assyria, after he had carried Israel away into captivity, placed in the cities of Samaria, that "they feared the Lord, and served their own gods." "These nations," saith the inspired writer, "feared the Lord;" performed an outward service to him (a plain proof that they had a fear of God, though not according to knowledge;) "and served their graven images, both their children, and their children's children: As did their fathers, so do they unto this day. (2 Kings 17:33.)
Already labelled grade 1 (unchanged): #28 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 8: «Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal»
column9:
1. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0039): «Consequently this care, to provide for ourselves and our household, this thought how to render to all their dues, our blessed Lord does not condemn. Yea, it is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour.» Reason: Reassures the money-worrier that sensible planning to provide for family is approved by God, not forbidden.
2. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0041): «He forbids only that care which poisons the blessings of to-day, by fear of what may be to-morrow; which cannot enjoy the present plenty, through apprehensions of future want.» Reason: Defines exactly the anxious care about tomorrow and future want that Christ forbids; names the asker's experience.
3. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0043): «Take no uneasy thought: This is a plain, sure rule, Uneasy care is unlawful care. With a single eye to God, do all that in you lies to provide things honest in the sight of all men. And then give up all into better hands; leave the whole event to God.» Reason: Direct practical rule for anxiety: do your honest part, then leave the outcome to God.
4. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0044): «If then God gave you life, the greater gift, will he not give you food to sustain it? If he hath given you the body, how can ye doubt but he will give you raiment to cover it?» Reason: Applies Christ's argument as a promise: God who gave life will provide food and clothing.
5. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0049): «But ye are sensible "your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things." And he hath pointed out to you an infallible way of being constantly supplied therewith» Reason: Promises the anxious that God knows their needs and gives a sure way to be supplied: seek his kingdom first.
6. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0060): «This care God hath taken upon himself: Cast you all your care upon Him. He knoweth your wants; and whatsoever is lacking he will not fail to supply.» Reason: Direct counsel to cast every care on God, who has promised to supply what is lacking.
7. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0063): «Why should you perplex yourself without need? God provides for you to-day what is needful to sustain the life which he hath given you. It is enough: Give yourself up into his hands. If you live another day, he will provide for that also.» Reason: Speaks straight to worry about tomorrow: God provides today and will provide tomorrow too.
8. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0075): «But when the temptation comes, the grace will come. In greater trials you will have greater strength. When sufferings abound, the consolations of God will, in the same proportion, abound also.» Reason: Answers fear of future trials: strength and grace are given when the trial actually comes.
9. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0076): «"Let the morrow," therefore, "take thought for the things of itself;" that is, when the morrow comes, then think of it. Live thou to-day. Be it thy earnest care to improve the present hour.» Reason: Plain counsel on taking thought for the future: think of tomorrow when it comes, live today.
10. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0080): «And he gives in one day, sufficient for that day; proportioned to the want and strength of the patient. If, therefore, thou snatchest to-day what belongs to the morrow; if thou addest this to what is given thee already, it will be more than thou canst bear» Reason: Explains why borrowing tomorrow's troubles crushes us: God apportions each day's burden to that day's strength.
11. #105 On Conscience (wesley-105-c0046): «O how quiet, as well as holy, would our lives be, had we learned that single lesson, -- to be careful for nothing, but to do our duty, and leave all consequences to God!» Reason: Counsel against anxious foreboding: do your duty and leave consequences to God for a quiet life.

column5: How can I know that I am really a child of God? What did Wesley teach about the assurance of salvation?
column7: #10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I
column8:
#10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I, wesley-010-c0021: 7. But what is that testimony of God's Spirit, which is superadded to, and conjoined with, this? How does he "bear witness with our spirit that we are the children of God?" It is hard to find words in the language of men to explain "the deep things of God." Indeed, there are none that will adequately express what the children of God experience. But perhaps one might say, (desiring any who are taught of God to correct, to soften or strengthen the expression,) «The testimony of the Spirit is an inward impression on the soul, whereby the Spirit of God directly witnesses to my spirit, that I am a child of God; that Jesus Christ hath loved me, and given himself for me; and that all my sins are blotted out, and I, even I, am reconciled to God.»
Already labelled grade 1 (unchanged): #11 The Witness of the Spirit, Discourse II: «To secure us from all delusion, God gives us two witnesses that we are his children.»
column9:
1. #10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I (wesley-010-c0009): «every man applying those scriptural marks to himself, may know whether he is a child of God.» Reason: Answers 'how can I know': apply Scripture's marks of God's children to yourself and draw the conclusion.
2. #10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I (wesley-010-c0016): «By the same immediate consciousness, you will know if your soul is alive to God; if you are saved from the pain of proud wrath, and have the ease of a meek and quiet spirit. By the same means you cannot but perceive if you love, rejoice, and delight in God.» Reason: Explains how a believer knows he has the marks: by immediate inner consciousness, as we know we are alive.
3. #10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I (wesley-010-c0025): «We know that we love God and keep his commandments; and "hereby also we know that we are of God." This is that testimony of our own spirit, which, so long as we continue to love God and keep his commandments, continues joined with the testimony of God's Spirit» Reason: Describes the joint witness of God's Spirit and our own spirit by which we know we are God's children.
4. #10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I (wesley-010-c0030): «But I thus love, delight, and rejoice in God; Therefore, I am a child of God: -- Then a Christian can in no wise doubt of his being a child of God.» Reason: Gives the reasoning by which a believer can be sure he is a child of God without doubt.
5. #10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I (wesley-010-c0032): «the Spirit of God does give a believer such a testimony of his adoption that while it is present to the soul, he can no more doubt the reality of his sonship, than he can doubt of the shining of the sun» Reason: Affirms that God's Spirit gives believers a testimony of adoption that removes doubt, the heart of Wesley's assurance.
6. #10 THE WITNESS OF THE SPIRIT, Discourse I (wesley-010-c0061): «By the fruits which he hath wrought in your spirit, you shall know the testimony of the Spirit of God. Hereby you shall know, that you are in no delusion, that you have not deceived your own soul.» Reason: Tells the asker how to be sure their assurance is real and not self-deception: look for the Spirit's fruits.
7. #11 The Witness of the Spirit, Discourse II (wesley-011-c0012): «The word of God says, every one who has the fruit of the Spirit is a child of God; experience, or inward consciousness, tells me, that I have the fruit of the Spirit; and hence I rationally conclude, "Therefore I am a child of God."» Reason: Lays out the indirect witness: Scripture plus inner experience lets one conclude 'I am a child of God.'
8. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0020): «And it is certain, this faith necessarily implies an assurance (which is here only another word for evidence, it being hard to tell the difference between them) that Christ loved me, and gave Himself for me.» Reason: Teaches that saving faith itself carries assurance that Christ loved me; core of Wesley's doctrine of assurance.
9. #106 On Faith (wesley-106-c0024): «It might have been said, (and it is all that can be said with propriety,) "Hitherto you are only a servant, you are not a child of God. You have already great reason to praise God that he has called you to his honourable service. Fear not.» Reason: Pastoral word to one lacking assurance: not condemned, a servant of God, to keep seeking and not fear.
10. #106 On Faith (wesley-106-c0025): «Thus, the faith of a child is, properly and directly, a divine conviction, whereby every child of God is enabled to testify, "The life that I now live, I live by faith the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me."» Reason: Defines the faith of a child of God as a divine conviction of Christ's personal love, witnessed by the Spirit.
11. #128 Free Grace (wesley-128-c0026): «And it does indeed imply a full assurance that all your past sins are forgiven, and that you are now a child of God. But it does not necessarily imply a full assurance of our future perseverance.» Reason: Clarifies what assurance covers: present sonship and forgiven sins, not necessarily future perseverance.
12. #18 The Marks of the New Birth (wesley-018-c0047): «The question is not, what you was made in baptism; (do not evade;) but, What are you now? Is the Spirit of adoption now in your heart? To your own heart let the appeal be made.» Reason: Direct self-examination for the asker: are you a child of God now, by the Spirit of adoption in your heart.
13. #72 Of Evil Angels (wesley-072-c0053): «If he inject doubts whether you are a child of God, or fears lest you should not endure to the end; "take to you for a helmet the hope of salvation."» Reason: Counsel for someone troubled by doubts whether they are God's child: hold fast the hope of salvation.
14. #11 The Witness of the Spirit, Discourse II (wesley-011-c0009): «the stormy wind and troubled waves subside, and there is a sweet calm; the heart resting as in the arms of Jesus, and the sinner being clearly satisfied that God is reconciled, that all his "iniquities are forgiven, and his sins covered."» Reason: Describes the Spirit's direct witness: an inner calm in which the believer is clearly satisfied his sins are forgiven.
15. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0025): «They are daily sensible of sin remaining in their heart, -- pride, self-will, unbelief; and of sin cleaving to all they speak and do, even their best actions and holiest duties. Yet at the same time they "know that they are of God;" they cannot doubt of it for a moment.» Reason: Shows believers can be sure they are God's children even while still feeling sin in themselves.
16. #21 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 1 (wesley-021-c0066): «And, if then, instead of immediately crying to God, they reason with him that is wiser than they, they will be in heaviness indeed, in sorrow of heart, in anguish not to be expressed.» Reason: Explains why forgiven people later doubt it (the tempter calls it a delusion) and counsels crying to God rather than arguing.
17. #62 The End of Christ's Coming (wesley-062-c0043): «"Being justified by faith, we have peace with God, through our Lord Jesus Christ;" -- that peace which enables us in every state therewith to be content; which delivers us from all perplexing doubts» Reason: Says believers know they are God's children by a direct view, with a peace that delivers from perplexing doubts.

column5: Is it wrong for a Christian to try to earn more money? What did Wesley say about making a living?
column8: #50 The Use of Money, wesley-050-c0011: It is therefore of the highest concern that all who fear God know how to employ this valuable talent; that they be instructed how it may answer these glorious ends, and in the highest degree. And, perhaps, all the instructions which are necessary for this may be reduced to three plain rules, by the exact observance whereof we may approve ourselves faithful stewards of "the mammon of unrighteousness." I. 1. The first of these is «(he that heareth, let him understand!) "Gain all you can." Here we may speak like the children of the world: We meet them on their own ground.» And it is our bounden duty to do this: We ought to gain all we can gain, without buying gold too dear, without paying more for it than it is worth.
column9:
1. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0006): «"The love of money," we know, "is the root of all evil;" but not the thing itself. The fault does not lie in the money, but in them that use it.» Reason: Answers whether earning money is wrong: money itself is not evil, only the love and misuse of it.
2. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0018): «These, likewise, are sacredly to be avoided, whatever gain they may be attended with provided we follow the custom of the trade; for to gain money we must not lose our souls.» Reason: Sets the limit on earning: no work requiring cheating or lying, whatever it pays.
3. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0022): «We cannot, consistent with brotherly love, sell our goods below the market price; we cannot study to ruin our neighbour's trade, in order to advance our own» Reason: Speaks to getting ahead: we may not advance ourselves by hurting a neighbour's business.
4. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0032): «it is the bounden duty of all who are engaged in worldly business to observe that first and great rule of Christian wisdom with respect to money, "Gain all you can." Gain all you can by honest industry. Use all possible diligence in your calling.» Reason: Says hard, honest work to earn is a Christian duty, not something to avoid.
5. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0050): «he placed you here not as a proprietor, but a steward: As such he entrusted you, for a season, with goods of various kinds; but the sole property of these still rests in him» Reason: Gives the frame for earning: what we gain is God's, held as stewards, which shapes why we work.
6. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0061): «Gain all you can, without hurting either yourself or your neighbour, in soul or body, by applying hereto with unintermitted diligence, and with all the understanding which God has given you» Reason: Wesley's summary rule for making a living: earn diligently without harm, then save and give.
7. #28 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 8 (wesley-028-c0002): «If a man pursues his business that he may raise himself to a state of honour and riches in the world, he is no longer serving God in his employment» Reason: Answers 'getting ahead': work pursued to rise in wealth and honour is no longer serving God.
8. #28 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 8 (wesley-028-c0071): «How then is it possible for a rich man to grow richer without denying the Lord that bought him? Yea, how can any man who has already the necessaries of life gain or aim at more, and be guiltless?» Reason: Sharp warning against aiming at more once needs are met, tied to Christ's command not to lay up treasure.
9. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0038): «It is the will of God, that every man should labour to eat his own bread; yea, and that every man should provide for his own, for them of his own household.» Reason: Affirms that working to support oneself and family is God's will.
10. #68 The Wisdom of God's Counsels (wesley-068-c0041): «They gain all they can, honestly and conscientiously. 2. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0018): «These, likewise, are sacredly to be avoided, whatever gain they may be attended with provided we follow the custom of the trade; for to gain money we must not lose our souls.» Reason: Sets the limit on earning: no work requiring cheating or lying, whatever it pays.
3. #50 The Use of Money (wesley-050-c0022): «We cannot, consistent with brotherly love, sell our goods below the market price; we cannot study to ruin our neighbour's trade, in order to advance our own» Reason: Speaks to getting ahead: we may not advance ourselves by hurting a neighbour's business.

column5: Can a Christian be wealthy without it hurting their soul? What did Wesley say about the danger of riches?
column8:
#87 The Danger of Riches, wesley-087-c0000: "«They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful desires, which drown men in destruction and perdition.»" 1 Tim. 6:9. 1. How innumerable are the ill consequences which have followed from men's not knowing, or not considering, this great truth! And how few are there even in the Christian world, that either know or duly consider it! Yea, how small is the number of those, even among real Christians, who understand and lay it to heart! Most of these too pass it very lightly over, scarce remembering there is such a text in the Bible. And many put such a construction upon it, as makes it of no manner of effect.
Already labelled grade 1 (unchanged): #108 On Riches: «How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God! It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God»
column9:
1. #28 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 8 (wesley-028-c0047): «For a man may possibly be rich, without any fault of his, by an overruling Providence, preventing his own choice: But he affirms it of hoi boulomenoi plourein, those who desire or seek to be rich.» Reason: Distinguishes having riches, which may be no fault, from desiring them, which destroys the soul.
2. #61 The Mystery of Iniquity (wesley-061-c0072): «Not that money is an evil of itself: It is applicable to good as well as bad purposes. But, nevertheless, it is an undoubted truth, that "the love of money is the root of all evil;" and also, that the possession of riches naturally breeds the love of them.» Reason: Explains the danger: money is not evil, but possessing riches naturally breeds the love of them.
3. #68 The Wisdom of God's Counsels (wesley-068-c0034): «And yet I have not known threescore rich persons, perhaps not half the number, during threescore years, who, as far as I can judge, were not less holy than they would have been had they been poor.» Reason: Wesley's long observation that riches nearly always made people less holy; defines rich as having something over.
4. #68 The Wisdom of God's Counsels (wesley-068-c0042): «But they do not give all they can; without which they must needs grow more and more earthly-minded. Their affections will cleave to the dust more and more; and they will have less and less communion with God. Is not this your case?» Reason: Shows how surplus hurts the soul when not given away: more earthly-minded, less communion with God.
5. #87 The Danger of Riches (wesley-087-c0015): «But to lay up any more, when this is done, is what our Lord has flatly forbidden. When it is calmly and deliberately done, it is a clear proof of our desiring to be rich.» Reason: Answers the person with more than they need: providing for family is allowed, hoarding the surplus is forbidden.
6. #87 The Danger of Riches (wesley-087-c0035): «Riches, either desired or possessed, naturally lead to some or other of these foolish and hurtful desires; and by affording the means of gratifying them all, naturally tend to increase them.» Reason: Explains how wealth harms the soul: it feeds and multiplies foolish, hurtful desires and evil tempers.
7. #87 The Danger of Riches (wesley-087-c0044): «I answer, It is possible. You may gain all you can without hurting either your soul or body; you may save all you can, by carefully avoiding every needless expense; and yet never lay up treasures on earth» Reason: Directly answers whether one can prosper without spiritual harm: yes, by never hoarding the surplus.
8. #87 The Danger of Riches (wesley-087-c0046): «But the Apostle does not fix the charge, barely on possessing any quantity of goods, but on possessing more than we employ according to the will of the Donor.» Reason: Clarifies that wealth itself is not the sin; keeping more than one uses as God wills is.
9. #87 The Danger of Riches (wesley-087-c0048): «Herein, my brethren, let you that are rich, be even as I am. Do you that possess more than food and raiment ask: "What shall we do? Shall we throw into the sea what God hath given us?" God forbid that you should! It is an excellent talent» Reason: Direct counsel to those with more than they need: do not throw it away; use it as a talent for God.
10. #87 The Danger of Riches (wesley-087-c0060): «Have you the same vehement desire as you formerly had, of "going on unto perfection?" Have they not hurt you by weakening your faith?» Reason: Self-examination for the prosperous: have riches already weakened your hunger for God and your faith?
11. #108 On Riches (wesley-108-c0011): «Or if you take faith, in the proper Christian sense, as a divine confidence in a pardoning God; what a deadly, what an almost insuperable, hinderance to this faith are riches!» Reason: Names a specific spiritual harm of wealth: it hinders humble faith in a pardoning God.
12. #108 On Riches (wesley-108-c0014): «Riches are equally a hinderance to the loving our neighbour as ourselves; that is, to the loving all mankind as Christ loved us.» Reason: Names another harm of riches: they hinder love of neighbour and humility.
13. #112 The Rich Man and Lazarus (wesley-112-c0031): «And it is no more sinful to be rich than to be poor. But it is dangerous beyond expression. Therefore, I remind all of you that are of this number, that have the conveniences of life, and something over that ye walk upon slippery ground.» Reason: Direct answer: being rich is not sinful in itself, but extremely dangerous to the soul.
14. #116 Causes of the Inefficacy of Christianity (wesley-116-c0043): «And it is an observation which admits of few exceptions, that nine in ten of these decreased in grace, in the same proportion as they increased in wealth.» Reason: Wesley's observation that growing wealth usually brought declining grace.
15. #116 Causes of the Inefficacy of Christianity (wesley-116-c0046): «I can see only one possible way; find out another who can. Do you gain all you can, and save all you can? Then you must, in the nature of things, grow rich. Then if you have any desire to escape the damnation of hell, give all you can» Reason: Asks the asker's question and gives Wesley's one remedy: having gained and saved, give all you can.
16. #126 On the Danger of Increasing Riches (wesley-126-c0001): «It is true, riches, and the increase of them, are the gift of God. Yet great care is to be taken, that what is intended for a blessing, do not turn into a curse.» Reason: Says increasing riches are God's gift but can turn into a curse; directly frames the asker's situation.
17. #126 On the Danger of Increasing Riches (wesley-126-c0016): «unless thy charities increase in the same proportion; unless thou givest a full tenth of thy substance, of thy fixed and occasional income; thou dost undoubtedly set thy heart upon thy gold» Reason: Gives a concrete test for the prosperous: if giving does not grow with income, your heart is set on gold.
18. #126 On the Danger of Increasing Riches (wesley-126-c0020): «Riches have increased with thee; at the peril of thy soul, "set not thine heart upon them!" Be thankful to Him that gave thee such a talent, so much power of doing good. Yet dare not to rejoice over them, but with fear and trembling.» Reason: Direct counsel to one whose riches increased: be thankful, use them for good, never set your heart on them.
19. #126 On the Danger of Increasing Riches (wesley-126-c0039): «Secondly. Hoard nothing. Lay up no treasure on earth, but give all you can; that is, all you have. I defy all the men upon earth, yea, all the angels in heaven, to find any other way of extracting the poison from riches.» Reason: Wesley's remedy for the spiritual poison of wealth: spend nothing on vanity, hoard nothing, give all you can.

column5: How should I pray when I am alone? What did Wesley say about private prayer?
column7: #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6
column8: #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6, wesley-026-c0001: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. «But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret, he shall reward thee openly.» But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the Heathen do: For they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. Be not ye therefore like unto them: For your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before you ask him.
column9:
1. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0037): «A direction, equally full and express, to wait for the blessings of God in private prayer, together with a positive promise, that, by this means, we shall obtain the request of our lips» Reason: Wesley calls private prayer a direct command of Christ with a promise attached; answers why and that one should pray alone.
2. #24 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 4 (wesley-024-c0013): «We have need daily to retire from the world, at least morning and evening, to converse with God, to commune more freely with our Father which is in secret.» Reason: Practical counsel: withdraw daily, morning and evening, to commune with God in secret.
3. #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6 (wesley-026-c0018): «Prayer is the lifting up of the heart to God: All words of prayer, without this, are mere hypocrisy. Whenever therefore thou attemptest to pray, see that it be thy one design to commune with God» Reason: Explains how to pray: sincerely lifting the heart to God, aiming only at communion with him, not at being seen.
4. #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6 (wesley-026-c0022): «Use all the privacy thou canst. (Only leave it not undone, whether thou hast any closet, any privacy, or no. Pray to God, if it be possible, when none seeth but He; but, if otherwise, pray to God.)» Reason: Wesley's exposition of the closet text: seek privacy, but pray regardless; pour out your heart to the Father in secret.
5. #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6 (wesley-026-c0024): «Do not use abundance of words without any meaning. Say not the same thing over and over again; think not the fruit of your prayers depends on the length of them» Reason: Direct counsel for secret prayer: avoid empty repetition and wordiness.
6. #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6 (wesley-026-c0026): «So that the end of your praying is not to inform God, as though he knew not your wants already; but rather to inform yourselves; to fix the sense of those wants more deeply in your hearts» Reason: Explains what prayer is for: deepening our sense of need and dependence, readying us to receive.
7. #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6 (wesley-026-c0028): «our Lord subjoins an example of it; even that divine form of prayer which seems in this place to be proposed by way of pattern chiefly, as the model and standard of all our prayers» Reason: Points the asker to the Lord's Prayer as the model for how to pray, containing all we need to ask.
8. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0023): «Perhaps no sin of omission more frequently occasions this than the neglect of private prayer; the want whereof cannot be supplied by any other ordinance whatever.» Reason: Says private prayer is irreplaceable and its neglect brings spiritual darkness; strong reason to keep it.
9. #89 The More Excellent Way (wesley-089-c0021): «Consider both your outward and inward state, and vary your prayers accordingly.» Reason: Practical advice on ordering private devotions: suit your prayers to your circumstances rather than repeating one form.
10. #25 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 5 (wesley-025-c0075): «Are you zealous of, and diligent in, private prayer? Do you suffer no day to pass without it?» Reason: Exhorts daily, unhurried private prayer and challenges those who give it little time.

column5: Someone hurt me and I cannot let it go. What did Wesley say about forgiving people who wrong us?
column7: #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6
column8: #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6, wesley-026-c0003: And forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen. «For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.»" Matt. 6:1-15. 1. In the preceding chapter our Lord has described inward religion in its various branches. He has laid before us those dispositions of soul which constitute real Christianity; the inward tempers contained in that "holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord;" the affections which, when flowing from their proper fountain, from a living faith in God through Christ Jesus, are intrinsically and essentially good, and acceptable to God.
column9:
1. #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6 (wesley-026-c0072): «So that if any malice or bitterness, if any taint of unkindness or anger remains, if we do not clearly, fully, and from the heart, forgive all men their trespasses, we far cut short the forgiveness of our own» Reason: Explains that lingering bitterness limits God's forgiveness of us; we must forgive fully and from the heart.
2. #26 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 6 (wesley-026-c0075): «Now, even now, by his grace, forgive as you would be forgiven! Now have compassion on thy fellow-servant, as God hath had and will have pity on thee!» Reason: Direct exhortation to forgive now, by God's grace, remembering the pity God has shown you.
3. #23 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 3 (wesley-023-c0080): «If you can do nothing more, at least "pray for them that despitefully use you and persecute you." You can never be disabled from doing this; nor can all their malice or violence hinder you.» Reason: Practical counsel toward those who wrong us: pray for them always, forgive the repentant fully, wrestle with God for the unrepentant.
4. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0055): «Have you not been offended at any of your brethren, looking at their (real or imagined) sin, so as to sin yourself against the great law of love, by estranging your heart from them? Then look unto the Lord» Reason: Addresses holding offence against others: it estranges the heart; look to the Lord so love returns and you forgive as God forgave.

column5: What does Wesley mean by Christian perfection? Can a believer be made perfect in this life?
column8:
#40 Christian Perfection, wesley-040-c0023: 9. «Christian perfection, therefore, does not imply (as some men seem to have imagined) an exemption either from ignorance or mistake, or infirmities or temptations. Indeed, it is only another term for holiness.» They are two names for the same thing. Thus every one that is perfect is holy, and every one that is holy is, in the Scripture sense, perfect. Yet we may, lastly, observe, that neither in this respect is there any absolute perfection on earth. There is no perfection of degrees, as it is termed; none which does not admit of a continual increase. So that how much soever any man hath attained, or in how high a degree soever he is perfect, he hath still need to "grow in grace," [2 Pet. 3:18] and daily to advance in the knowledge and love of God his Saviour. [see Phil. 1:9]
Already labelled grade 1 (unchanged): #76 On Perfection: «leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection»
column9:
1. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0015): «But what is perfection? The word has various senses: here it means perfect love. It is love excluding sin; love filling the heart, taking up the whole capacity of the soul.» Reason: Direct definition: Christian perfection is perfect love that excludes sin and fills the whole heart.
2. #76 On Perfection (wesley-076-c0012): «What is then the perfection of which man is capable while he dwells in a corruptible body? It is the complying with that kind command, "My son, give me thy heart."» Reason: Answers what perfection is possible in this life: loving God with all the heart, summed up in love.
3. #76 On Perfection (wesley-076-c0019): «According to this Apostle, then, perfection is another name for universal holiness: Inward and outward righteousness: Holiness of life, arising from holiness of heart.» Reason: Defines Christian perfection as universal holiness of heart and life.
4. #76 On Perfection (wesley-076-c0044): «Why cannot the Almighty sanctify the soul while it is in the body? Cannot he sanctify you while you are in this house, as well as in the open air?» Reason: Argues God can save from all sin before death, and has promised it in the command to love him wholly.
5. #83 On Patience (wesley-083-c0042): «Believe, Fourthly, that he is not only able, but willing to do it now. Not when you come to die; not at any distant time; not to-morrow, but to-day.» Reason: Says God can purify from all sin and fill the heart with love now, not at death; direct counsel to the seeker.
6. #40 Christian Perfection (wesley-040-c0084): «In conformity, therefore, both to the doctrine of St. John, and to the whole tenor of the New Testament, we fix this conclusion -- A Christian is so far perfect, as not to commit sin.» Reason: States in what sense a believer is perfect in this life: not committing sin, and for mature believers freedom from evil tempers.
7. #40 Christian Perfection (wesley-040-c0098): «"True," say some, "we shall thus be saved from our sins; but not till death; not in this world." But how are we to reconcile this with the express words of St. John?» Reason: Answers the 'only at death' objection: Scripture says believers are saved from sin in this world.
8. #40 Christian Perfection (wesley-040-c0105): «It remains, then, that Christians are saved in this world from all sin, from all unrighteousness; that they are now in such a sense perfect, as not to commit sin, and to be freed from evil thoughts and evil tempers.» Reason: Wesley's summary conclusion: believers can be perfect in this life, freed from sin, evil thoughts and tempers.
9. #40 Christian Perfection (wesley-040-c0061): «No necessity of sinning was laid upon them. The grace of God was surely sufficient for them. And it is sufficient for us at this day.» Reason: Denies that Christians must keep sinning; grace is sufficient and no one need yield to temptation.
10. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0003): «We expect to be "made perfect in love;" in that love which casts out all painful fear, and all desire but that of glorifying him we love, and of loving and serving him more and more.» Reason: Describes the expected perfection in love: freedom from fear, anger, pride, and unkind tempers.
11. #110 On the Discoveries of Faith (wesley-110-c0034): «But what is the "perfection" here spoken of? It is not only a deliverance from doubts and fears, but from sin; from all inward as well as outward sin» Reason: Direct definition of perfection as deliverance from all inward and outward sin.
12. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0054): «Admitting, therefore, that "with men it is impossible" to "bring a clean thing out of an unclean," to purify the heart from all sin, and to till it with all holiness; yet this creates no difficulty in the case» Reason: Answers 'is it possible': purifying the heart from all sin is impossible to us but possible to God.
13. #19 The Great Privilege of those that are Born of God (wesley-019-c0055): «Watch, that thou mayest pray without ceasing, at all times, and in all places, pouring out thy heart before him! So shalt thou always believe, and always love, and never commit sin.» Reason: Practical counsel: by watching and praying the believer may continue in love and not commit sin.
14. #85 On Working out our own Salvation (wesley-085-c0034): «Since he worketh in you of his own good pleasure, without any merit of yours, both to will and to do, it is possible for you to fulfil all righteousness.» Reason: Says God's working in us makes it possible to fulfil all righteousness and love God.

column5: I have been sad for a long time and my faith feels heavy. What did Wesley say about heaviness and sorrow in a believer?
column8: #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations, wesley-047-c0000: "Now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations." 1 Pet. 1:6. 1. In the preceding discourse I have particularly spoken of that darkness of mind into which those are often observed to fall who once walked in the light of God's countenance. «Nearly related to this is the heaviness of soul which is still more common, even among believers.» Indeed, almost all the children of God experience this, in an higher or lower degree. And so great is the resemblance between one and the other, that they are frequently confounded together; and we are apt to say, indifferently, "Such an one is in darkness," or "Such an one is in heaviness;" -- as if they were equivalent terms, one of which implied no more than the other.
column9:
1. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0003): «At the same time, therefore, that they were "in heaviness," they were possessed of living faith.» Reason: Shows from 1 Peter that those in heaviness were true believers; heaviness does not mean faith is gone.
2. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0010): «So that, upon the whole, their heaviness well consisted with faith, with hope, with love of God and man, with the peace of God, with joy in the Holy Ghost, with inward and outward holiness.» Reason: Direct answer: a believer's heaviness is compatible with faith, hope, love, peace and holiness.
3. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0014): «Neither does this appear to be a transient sorrow, such as passes away in an hour; but rather, such as, having taken fast hold of the heart, is not presently shaken off, but continues for some time» Reason: Says believers' heaviness can be deep and long-lasting even with living faith; speaks to sadness lasting months.
4. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0015): «It may likewise have an influence over the body; particularly in those that are either of a naturally weak constitution, or weakened by some accidental disorder, especially of the nervous kind.» Reason: Explains that lasting sorrow can affect body and nerves yet still consist with faith working by love.
5. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0017): «But to proceed to the Third point: What are the causes of such sorrow or heaviness in a true believer? The Apostle tells us clearly: "Ye are in heaviness," says he, "through manifold temptations,"» Reason: Names the cause of a true believer's heaviness: manifold trials; those in heaviness are sorrowful yet rejoicing.
6. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0021): «And faith does not overturn the course of nature: Natural causes still produce natural effects. Faith no more hinders the sinking of the spirits (as it is called) in an hysteric illness than the rising of the pulse in a fever.» Reason: Low spirits from long illness or nervous disorders are natural effects, not a failure of faith.
7. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0030): «In all these cases, we not only may, but ought to, be affected: It is the design of God that we should. He would not have us stocks and stones. He would have our affections regulated, not extinguished.» Reason: Grief over loss is God's design; 'there may be sorrow without sin' answers 'is something wrong with me'.
8. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0035): «Certainly he will do this, if we grieve his Holy Spirit, either by outward or inward sin; either by doing evil, or neglecting to do good; by giving way either to pride or anger, to spiritual sloth» Reason: Explains whether God withdraws from the sorrowing soul: never arbitrarily, only when his Spirit is grieved by sin.
9. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0044): «Hence we learn, that the first and great end of God's permitting the temptations which bring heaviness on his children, Is the trial of their faith, which is tried by these, even as gold by the fire.» Reason: Gives God's purpose in permitting heaviness: to purify and strengthen faith like gold in fire.
10. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0056): «Darkness, or the wilderness-state, implies a total loss of joy in the Holy Ghost: Heaviness does not; in the midst of this we may "rejoice with joy unspeakable."» Reason: Distinguishes heaviness from spiritual darkness, reassuring the heavy believer they have not lost peace or love.
11. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0058): «There may be need of our being in "heaviness for a season," in order to the ends above recited» Reason: Says heaviness may be needful for a season, to try faith, enlarge hope and perfect love.
12. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0062): «But we need not be solicitous how to avoid so much as how to improve by heaviness. Our great care should be, so to behave ourselves under it, so to wait upon the Lord therein» Reason: Direct counsel: wait on the Lord and use heaviness to grow in faith, hope and holiness.
13. #21 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 1 (wesley-021-c0063): «But he now "hides his face, and they are troubled:" They cannot see him through the dark cloud.» Reason: Describes the believer who mourns after God when he seems hidden, and why trouble and heaviness take hold.
14. #21 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 1 (wesley-021-c0068): «Sure it is, that this "affliction," for the present, "is not joyous, but grievous; nevertheless afterward it bringeth forth peaceable fruit unto them that are exercised thereby." Blessed, therefore, are they that thus mourn, if they "tarry the Lord's leisure,"» Reason: Promise and counsel to mourning believers: the grief bears fruit if they wait on the Lord and refuse worldly comforts.
15. #21 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 1 (wesley-021-c0071): «"And ye shall be sorrowful," through doubt, through fear, through temptation, through vehement desire; "but your sorrow shall be turned into joy," by the return of Him whom your soul loveth.» Reason: Applies Christ's promise to believers mourning an absent God: their sorrow will be turned into joy.
16. #89 The More Excellent Way (wesley-089-c0023): «Is your soul in heaviness, either from a sense of sin, or through manifold temptations? Then let your prayer consist of such confessions, petitions, and supplications, as are agreeable to your distressed situation of mind.» Reason: Practical counsel for a soul in heaviness: pray honestly according to your distressed state.

column5: My child died and I do not know how to grieve. What did Wesley say about mourning the dead?
column8: #135 On Mourning for the Dead, wesley-135-c0000: "«Now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.»" 2 Sam. 12:23. The resolution of a wise and good man, just recovering the use of his reason and virtue, after the bitterness of soul he had tasted from the hourly expectation of the death of a beloved son, is comprised in these few but strong words. He had fasted and wept, and lay all night upon the earth, and refused not only comfort, but even needful sustenance, whilst the child was still alive, in hopes that God would be gracious, as well in that as in other instances, and reverse the just sentence he had pronounced.
column9:
1. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0005): «Be it my comfort, my constant comfort, when my sorrows bear hard upon me, that I shall shortly, very shortly, go to him! that I shall soon awake from this tedious dream of life» Reason: The bereaved parent's comfort: the child cannot return, but the parent will go to him and see him again.
2. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0013): «It is the property of envy, not of love, to repine at another's happiness; to weep, because all tears are wiped from their eyes.» Reason: Reframes grief for the dead: the loved one has reached their home and rest, so weep for ourselves, not them.
3. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0015): «Revelation tells us, that all occurrences of life must be borne with patience and moderation» Reason: Counsels bearing loss with patience, humility and resignation, trusting that whatever happens is for our good.
4. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0016): «"I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep; that ye sorrow not, even as others who have no hope.» Reason: Applies 1 Thessalonians 4 to the bereaved: grieve with hope, since God will bring those who sleep in Jesus.
5. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0024): «Who then can conceive, much less describe, the strong emotion, the secret workings of soul which a parent feels on such an occasion?» Reason: Acknowledges a parent's grief and allows sorrow without blame, while urging that it not be prolonged.
6. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0026): «What can give us sufficient ease after that rupture, which has left such an aching void in our breasts? What, indeed, but the reflection already mentioned, which can never be inculcated too often, -- that we are hastening to him ourselves» Reason: Answers how to go on: the aching void is eased by remembering we will soon join the one we lost.
7. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0029): «If we are, at any time, in danger of being overcome by dwelling too long on the gloomy side of this prospect» Reason: Direct counsel when grief overwhelms: turn to the bright side, the resurrection and victory over death.
8. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0030): «In all these cases, we not only may, but ought to, be affected: It is the design of God that we should. He would not have us stocks and stones.» Reason: On the death of a beloved child: grieving is God's design, not a failing; 'there may be sorrow without sin.'

column8: #135 On Mourning for the Dead, wesley-135-c0000: "«Now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.»" 2 Sam. 12:23. He had fasted and wept, and lay all night upon the earth, and refused not only comfort, but even needful sustenance, whilst the child was still alive, in hopes that God would be gracious, as well in that as in other instances, and reverse the just sentence he had pronounced.
column9:
1. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0005): «Be it my comfort, my constant comfort, when my sorrows bear hard upon me, that I shall shortly, very shortly, go to him! that I shall soon awake from this tedious dream of life» Reason: The bereaved parent's comfort: the child cannot return, but the parent will go to him and see him again.
2. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0013): «It is the property of envy, not of love, to repine at another's happiness; to weep, because all tears are wiped from their eyes.» Reason: Reframes grief for the dead: the loved one has reached their home and rest, so weep for ourselves, not them.
3. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0015): «Revelation tells us, that all occurrences of life must be borne with patience and moderation» Reason: Counsels bearing loss with patience, humility and resignation, trusting that whatever happens is for our good.
4. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0016): «"I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep; that ye sorrow not, even as others who have no hope.» Reason: Applies 1 Thessalonians 4 to the bereaved: grieve with hope, since God will bring those who sleep in Jesus.
5. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0024): «Who then can conceive, much less describe, the strong emotion, the secret workings of soul which a parent feels on such an occasion?» Reason: Acknowledges a parent's grief and allows sorrow without blame, while urging that it not be prolonged.
6. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0026): «What can give us sufficient ease after that rupture, which has left such an aching void in our breasts? What, indeed, but the reflection already mentioned, which can never be inculcated too often, -- that we are hastening to him ourselves» Reason: Answers how to go on: the aching void is eased by remembering we will soon join the one we lost.
7. #135 On Mourning for the Dead (wesley-135-c0029): «If we are, at any time, in danger of being overcome by dwelling too long on the gloomy side of this prospect» Reason: Direct counsel when grief overwhelms: turn to the bright side, the resurrection and victory over death.
8. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0030): «In all these cases, we not only may, but ought to, be affected: It is the design of God that we should. He would not have us stocks and stones.» Reason: On the death of a beloved child: grieving is God's design, not a failing; 'there may be sorrow without sin.'

column5: I feel like the devil is attacking my faith. What did Wesley say about Satan's devices?
column8: #42 Satan's Devices, wesley-042-c0007: We trust in his promise who cannot lie, that the time will surely come, when, in every word and work, we shall do his blessed will on earth, as it is done in heaven; when all our conversation shall be seasoned with salt, all meet to minister grace to the hearers; when, whether we eat or drink, or whatever we do, it shall be done to the glory of God; when all our words and deeds shall be "in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks unto God, even the Father, through him." 5. «Now this is the grand device of Satan, to destroy the first work of God in the soul, or at least to hinder its increase, by our expectation of that greater work.»
column9:
1. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0010): «that subtle adversary often damps the joy we should otherwise feel in what we have already attained, by a perverse representation of what we have not attained» Reason: Names a specific device: Satan dampens joy by fixing our eyes on what we lack rather than what God has done.
2. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0012): «If he can prevail thus far, if he can damp our joy, he will soon attack our peace also. He will suggest, "Are you fit to see God?» Reason: Describes how Satan attacks peace by suggesting we are too unholy to be accepted by God.
3. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0024): «At the same time that our wise adversary endeavours to make our conviction of the necessity of perfect love an occasion of shaking our peace by doubts and fears, he endeavours to weaken, if not destroy, our faith.» Reason: Explains that Satan's aim is to weaken faith, since peace and holiness stand or fall with it.
4. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0030): «there is, many times, no spirit left in them; they could almost cry out, "With God this is impossible!" They are ready to give up both faith and hope» Reason: Describes exactly the losing heart the asker feels, as the effect of this temptation on earnest believers.
5. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0044): «You may cast back this dart upon his own head, while through the grace of God, the more you feel of your own vileness, the more you rejoice in confident hope, that all this shall be done away.» Reason: First counter-move: turn Satan's accusation into hope that God will finish the work.
6. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0047): «take the more earnest heed to hold fast that, "Not by works of righteousness which I have done, I am found in him; I am accepted in the Beloved» Reason: When Satan assaults peace, hold fast that acceptance rests on Christ's righteousness by faith, not our own.
7. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0050): «The more you are tempted to give up your shield, to cast away your faith, your confidence in his love, so much the more take heed that you hold fast that whereunto you have attained» Reason: Direct counsel for when the devil pushes you to abandon faith: hold fast your confidence in Christ's love.
8. #72 Of Evil Angels (wesley-072-c0028): «By this means he assaults our faith, our evidence of things unseen. He endeavours to weaken that hope full of immortality to which God had begotten us» Reason: Explains how the devil attacks believers' faith, hope, joy and especially love of God.
9. #72 Of Evil Angels (wesley-072-c0049): «And, First, as a general preservative against all the rage, the power, and subtlety of your great adversary, put on the panoply, "the whole armour of God," universal holiness.» Reason: Wesley's first defence against Satan's attacks: put on the whole armour of God.
10. #72 Of Evil Angels (wesley-072-c0053): «If he inject doubts whether you are a child of God, or fears lest you should not endure to the end; "take to you for a helmet the hope of salvation."» Reason: Counsel for devil-injected doubts about being God's child: hold fast the hope of salvation.
11. #72 Of Evil Angels (wesley-072-c0055): «"resist" him, "steadfast in the faith." Then is the time, having cried to the Strong for strength, to "stir up the gift of God that is in you;"» Reason: When Satan assaults, cry to God for strength and resist steadfast in faith, and he will flee.
12. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0044): «Particularly when we reason with this enemy, instead of instantly calling upon God, and casting ourselves upon Him, by simple faith» Reason: Practical counsel under attack: don't argue with the enemy; instantly call on God in simple faith.
13. #47 Heaviness through Manifold Temptations (wesley-047-c0034): «And if we attempt to fight him with his own weapons, if we begin to reason with him, more and more heaviness will undoubtedly ensue, if not utter darkness.» Reason: Satan tries to stir the heart against God when we are low; reasoning with him only deepens the darkness.
14. #19 The Great Privilege of those that are Born of God (wesley-019-c0049): «that if the loving eye of the soul be steadily fixed on God, the temptation soon vanishes away» Reason: How to avoid the snare of the devil: keep the soul's eye fixed on God and watch unto prayer.
15. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0053): «lest he tempt God, by thinking or saying, "This is insupportable; this is too hard; I can never get through it; my burden is heavier that I can bear." Not so; unless something is too hard for God.» Reason: Answers losing heart under temptation: God proportions the trial to our strength; ask and more is given.
16. #42 Satan's Devices (wesley-042-c0019): «if your eye be not steadily fixed on Him who hath borne all your sins, he will bring you again under that "fear of death,"» Reason: Warns how Satan wears down peace and joy with fear; the defence is keeping your eye fixed on Christ who bore your sins.
17. #78 Spiritual Idolatry (wesley-078-c0043): «You are not able to contend with the evil world, much less with your own evil heart; and least of all, with the powers of darkness. Cry, therefore, to the Strong for strength.» Reason: Direct counsel for resisting the pull of the world and temptation: do not trust your own strength; cry to God for strength.
18. #78 Spiritual Idolatry (wesley-078-c0047): «fight the good fight of faith; take the kingdom of heaven by violence!» Reason: Exhorts the believer to fight on and stand fast in Christ's liberty, doing all things through Christ who strengthens.
19. #19 The Great Privilege of those that are Born of God (wesley-019-c0055): «Thou, therefore, O man of God! watch always; that thou mayest always hear the voice of God! Watch, that thou mayest pray without ceasing» Reason: Counsel to those who stand: watch and pray always so that inward sin does not regain dominion.

column5: The temptation I am facing feels too strong to bear. What did Wesley say about God making a way to escape?
column8: #82 On Temptation, wesley-082-c0000: "«There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: And God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.»" 1 Cor. 10:13. 1. In the foregoing part of the chapter, the Apostle has been reciting, on the one hand, the unparalleled mercies of God to the Israelites; and, on the other, the unparalleled ingratitude of that disobedient and gainsaying people. [1 Cor. 10:1-10] And all these things, as the Apostle observes, "were written for our ensample;" [1 Cor. 10:11] that we might take warning from them, so as to avoid their grievous sins, and escape their terrible punishment.
column9:
1. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0028): «what a comfort it is to know, with the utmost certainty, that "God is faithful, who will not suffer us to be tempted above what we are able." He knoweth what our ability is, and cannot be mistaken.» Reason: Expounds the promise directly: God knows your strength and never lets temptation exceed it; comfort for one who feels overwhelmed.
2. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0033): «He sees exactly how much we can endure with our present degree of strength. And if this is not sufficient, he can increase it to whatever degree it pleases him.» Reason: God watches every temptation so it never exceeds our strength, and increases strength when needed; direct answer to 'too strong to bear'.
3. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0035): «It literally means a way out. And this God will either find our make; which He that hath all wisdom, as well as all power in heaven and earth, can never be at a loss how to do.» Reason: Explains the 'way to escape': God always finds or makes a way out, either removing the occasion or changing it.
4. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0044): «Thus is God able to deliver out of temptation, by taking away the very ground of it. And he is equally able to deliver in the temptation; which, perhaps, is the greatest deliverance of all.» Reason: Describes the two ways God makes escape: removing the temptation or taking away its power while it remains.
5. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0054): «"This is insupportable; this is too hard; I can never get through it; my burden is heavier that I can bear." Not so; unless something is too hard for God. He will not suffer you to be "tempted above that ye are able."» Reason: Speaks straight to someone saying 'I can't bear this': God proportions the burden to your strength; ask for more strength.
6. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0055): «Let us then receive every trial with calm resignation, and with humble confidence that He who hath all power, all wisdom, all mercy, and all faithfulness, will first support us in every temptation, and then deliver us out of all» Reason: Practical counsel: trust God's faithfulness; he will support us in every temptation and then deliver us.
7. #29 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 9 (wesley-029-c0075): «But when the temptation comes, the grace will come. In greater trials you will have greater strength.» Reason: Promises grace arrives with the temptation and God makes a way to escape; direct comfort to one fearing they are too weak.
8. #40 Christian Perfection (wesley-040-c0061): «With the temptation which fell on them, there was a way to escape; as there is to every soul of man in every temptation. So that whosoever is tempted to any sin, need not yield» Reason: Applies 1 Cor 10:13: there is a way to escape in every temptation, so no one tempted need yield to sin.
9. #80 On Friendship with the World (wesley-080-c0043): «This is such a temptation as no power of man is able to overcome. Nothing less than the mighty power of God can make a way for you to escape from it. And this can work a complete deliverance: His grace is sufficient for you.» Reason: For a temptation too strong for human power, God's power makes the escape, if we cooperate and cut off the occasion.
10. #68 The Wisdom of God's Counsels (wesley-068-c0065): «Tempted you will be in ten thousand different ways, perhaps as long as you remain in the body; but as long as you continue to watch and pray, you will not "enter into temptations." His grace has been hitherto sufficient for you» Reason: Promises that by watching and praying you will not be overcome; God's grace is sufficient to the end.
11. #78 Spiritual Idolatry (wesley-078-c0043): «But do not either resolve, or attempt to execute your resolution, trusting in your own strength. If you do, you will be utterly foiled.» Reason: Counsel for breaking free of what pulls you from God: not by your own strength, but crying to God for strength.
12. #72 Of Evil Angels (wesley-072-c0055): «Then is the time, having cried to the Strong for strength, to "stir up the gift of God that is in you;" to summon all your faith, and hope, and love; to turn the attack in the name of the Lord» Reason: Direct counsel when temptation assaults with full strength: cry to God, resist in faith, and the tempter will flee.
13. #85 On Working out our own Salvation (wesley-085-c0037): «Surely it is not so. You can do something, through Christ strengthening you. Stir up the spark of grace which is now in you, and he will give you more grace.» Reason: Answers 'I feel too weak': through Christ you can act, and using present grace brings more grace.
14. #14 The Repentance of Believers (wesley-014-c0068): «faith accepts all the help we stand in need of, from him that hath all power in heaven and earth. Repentance says, "Without him I can do nothing:" Faith says, "I can do all things through Christ strengthening me."» Reason: Knowing our own helplessness, faith receives God's help to overcome the enemies of the soul; answers 'will God help me?'.

column5: How often should a Christian receive the Lord's Supper? What did Wesley teach about communion?
column7: #101 The Duty of Constant Communion J.W.
column8: #101 The Duty of Constant Communion J.W., wesley-101-c0006: The grace of God given herein confirms to us the pardon of our sins, by enabling us to leave them. As our bodies are strengthened by bread and wine, so are our souls by these tokens of the body and blood of Christ. This is the food of our souls: This gives strength to perform our duty, and leads us on to perfection. If, therefore, we have any regard for the plain command of Christ, if we desire the pardon of our sins, if we wish for strength to believe, to love and obey God, then «we should neglect no opportunity of receiving the Lord's Supper; then we must never turn our backs on the feast which our Lord has prepared for us.»
column9:
1. #101 The Duty of Constant Communion J.W. (wesley-101-c0001): «it is the duty of every Christian to receive the Lord's Supper as often as he can. 1. The First reason why it is the duty of every Christian so to do is, because it is a plain command of Christ.» Reason: States Wesley's answer outright: receive as often as you can, because Christ plainly commands it.
2. #101 The Duty of Constant Communion J.W. (wesley-101-c0004): «A Second reason why every Christian should do this as often as he can, is, because the benefits of doing it are so great to all that do it in obedience to him» Reason: Gives the second reason for frequent communion: forgiveness and strengthening of the soul amid constant temptation.
3. #101 The Duty of Constant Communion J.W. (wesley-101-c0008): «obey God, and consult the good of his own soul, by communicating every time he can; like the first Christians, with whom the Christian sacrifice was a constant part of the Lord's day service.» Reason: Urges communicating every time possible, citing early Christians who received weekly or even daily.
4. #101 The Duty of Constant Communion J.W. (wesley-101-c0013): «For if we are not obliged to communicate constantly, by what argument can it be proved that we are obliged to communicate frequently? yea, more than once a year, or once in seven years, or once before we die?» Reason: Explains why Wesley says constant, not merely frequent, communion; answers whether occasional is enough.
5. #101 The Duty of Constant Communion J.W. column5: What are the means of grace, and do they actually help a person grow?
column8: #16 The Means of Grace, wesley-016-c0012: They have probably tried most outward means, and found no ease in them; it may be, more and more of remorse, and fear, and sorrow, and condemnation. It is easy, therefore, to persuade these, that it is better for them to abstain from all those means. They are already weary of striving (as it seems) in vain, of labouring in the fire; and are therefore glad of any pretence to cast aside that wherein their soul has no pleasure, to give over the painful strife, and sink down into an indolent inactivity. II. 1. In the following discourse, I propose to examine at large, whether there are any means of grace. «By "means of grace" I understand outward signs, words, or actions, ordained of God, and appointed for this end, to be the ordinary channels whereby he might convey to men, preventing, justifying, or sanctifying grace.»
column9:
1. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0015): «But we allow, that the whole value of the means depends on their actual subservience to the end of religion; that, consequently, all these means, when separate from the end, are less than nothing and vanity» Reason: Names the chief means (prayer, Scripture, Supper) and says their worth lies in actually leading to the knowledge and love of God.
2. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0018): «We know that there is no inherent power in the words that are spoken in prayer, in the letter of Scripture read, the sound thereof heard, or the bread and wine received in the Lord's Supper» Reason: Explains how they help: the power is God's alone, working through them, not in the practices themselves.
3. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0027): «all who desire the grace of God are to wait for it in the means which he hath ordained; in using, not in laying them aside.» Reason: Wesley's central answer: those seeking God should use the means, not abandon them.
4. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0045): «And that this is a means whereby God not only gives, but also confirms and increases, true wisdom, we learn from the words of St. Paul to Timothy» Reason: Says Bible reading is a means God uses to give and increase grace and wisdom; speaks to whether it helps growth.
5. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0053): «Is not the eating of that bread, and the drinking of that cup, the outward, visible means, whereby God conveys into our souls all that spiritual grace, that righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost» Reason: Explains the Lord's Supper as a real channel by which God conveys grace, not an empty ritual.
6. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0059): «looking for the blessing of God therein? believing, that if I wait in this way, I shall attain what otherwise I should not? So I do. And so I will, God being my helper, even to my life's end.» Reason: Wesley affirms he expects real blessing through the means because God promised it; directly answers whether they help.
7. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0084): «As to the manner of using them, whereon indeed it wholly depends whether they should convey any grace at all to the user; it behoves us, First, always to retain a lively sense, that God is above all means.» Reason: Says whether the means help depends on how we use them; begins Wesley's practical rules.
8. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0086): «It is, in itself, a poor, dead, empty thing: Separate from God, it is a dry leaf, a shadow.» Reason: Answers the 'just habits' worry: without God the practice is empty, but we use it because God bids and meets us there.
9. #16 The Means of Grace (wesley-016-c0088): «In using all means, seek God alone. In and through every outward thing, look singly to the power of his Spirit; and the merits of his Son. Beware you do not stick in the work itself» Reason: Practical counsel on keeping practices from becoming mere routine: seek God through them, use them as means.
10. #4 Scriptural Christianity (wesley-004-c0022): «so he continued daily in all the ordinances of God, the stated channels of his grace to man» Reason: Describes the early believer growing daily in grace by steadily using prayer, teaching and the Supper.
11. #37 The Nature of Enthusiasm (wesley-037-c0065): «God can give the end without any means at all; but you have no reason to think He will. Therefore constantly and carefully use all those means which He has appointed to be the ordinary channels of His grace.» Reason: Direct counsel: do not expect growth without the appointed means; use them constantly.
12. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0034): «if a man willingly neglect them, he cannot reasonably expect that he shall ever be sanctified; he cannot grow in grace, in the image of God» Reason: Says works of piety are necessary for growth; neglecting them stops growth and loses grace already given.
13. #84 The Important Question (wesley-084-c0028): «This may be an excellent help to religion; and everyone who desires to save his soul should attend them at all opportunities; yet it is possible you may attend them all your days, and still have no religion at all.» Reason: Balanced answer: church and sacrament truly help, but can become mere habit without the love of God.
14. #84 The Important Question (wesley-084-c0033): «It is plain, all these fruits of love are means of increasing the love from which they spring» Reason: Says prayer, Scripture and the Supper, done from love, increase that love; they draw us closer to God.
15. #92 On Zeal (wesley-092-c0017): «By these we exercise all holy tempers- by these we continually improve them, so that all these are real means of grace» Reason: Explains how means help growth: practising them exercises and improves holy tempers; lists works of piety.
16. #98 On Visiting the Sick (wesley-098-c0001): «Surely there are works of mercy, as well as works of piety, which are real means of grace. They are more especially such to those that perform them with a single eye.» Reason: Identifies the means of grace (piety and mercy) and says neglecting them loses grace; they genuinely help.

column5: If I cannot earn heaven, how is a person saved? What did Wesley say about salvation by faith?
column8: #1 Salvation by Faith, wesley-001-c0033: To the same effect are the words both preceding and following the text (Eph. 2:4ff.): "God, who is rich in mercy, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ (by grace ye are saved), that he might show the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus. «For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves." Of yourselves cometh neither your faith nor your salvation: "it is the gift of God;" the free, undeserved gift»; the faith through which ye are saved, as well as the salvation which he of his own good pleasure, his mere favour, annexes thereto.
column9:
1. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0002): «Wherewithal then shall a sinful man atone for any the least of his sins? With his own works? No. Were they ever so many or holy, they are not his own, but God's.» Reason: Answers 'I can never be good enough': our own works cannot atone for even the least sin.
2. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0003): «herein "God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died" to save us "By grace" then "are ye saved through faith." Grace is the source, faith the condition, of salvation.» Reason: Core summary: Christ died for us while sinners; we are saved by grace as source, faith as condition.
3. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0012): «Christian faith is then, not only an assent to the whole gospel of Christ, but also a full reliance on the blood of Christ; a trust in the merits of his life, death, and resurrection» Reason: Defines the saving faith: full reliance on Christ's blood and merits, not our own, as our salvation.
4. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0038): «True, to despair of being saved by their own works, their own merits, or righteousness. And so it ought; for none can trust in the merits of Christ, till he has utterly renounced his own.» Reason: Speaks to the despair of not being good enough: give up trusting your merits and trust Christ's.
5. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0040): «What! Mercy for all? For Zacchaeus, a public robber? For Mary Magdalene, a common harlot? Methinks I hear one say "Then I, even I, may hope for mercy!" And so thou mayest» Reason: Salvation by faith is comfort to self-condemned sinners: mercy is offered to all who call on him.
6. #3 Awake, Thou That Sleepest (wesley-003-c0035): «Alas! all this will never bring thee to God. It is in his account lighter than vanity. Dost thou know Jesus Christ, whom he hath sent? Hath he taught thee, that "by grace we are saved through faith» Reason: Moral goodness and reputation cannot bring us to God; salvation is by grace through faith, not works.
7. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0048): «there is no other way of obtaining a share in his merit than by faith in his name» Reason: States plainly that the only way to share in Christ's saving merit is faith in him; works without it profit nothing.
8. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0052): «suppose, I say, this sinner, helpless and hopeless, casts himself wholly on the mercy of God in Christ, (which indeed he cannot do but by the grace of God,) who can doubt but he is forgiven in that moment?» Reason: However lacking in good works, the sinner who casts himself on God's mercy in Christ is forgiven at once.
9. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0064): «Thou who feelest thou art just fit for hell, art just fit to advance his glory; the glory of his free grace, justifying the ungodly and him that worketh not. O come quickly! Believe in the Lord Jesus» Reason: Direct invitation to one who feels unworthy: God justifies the ungodly; believe and be reconciled to God.
10. #6 The Righteousness of Faith (wesley-006-c0049): «the only, means under heaven given to a man, whereby he may regain the favour of God, which is better than life itself, or the image of God, which is the true life of the soul, is the submitting to the "righteousness which is of faith,"» Reason: The only way to regain God's favour is to submit to the righteousness of faith by believing in Christ.
11. #6 The Righteousness of Faith (wesley-006-c0052): «Neither say in thy heart, "I cannot be accepted yet, because I am not good enough." Who is good enough -- who ever was -- to merit acceptance at God's hands?» Reason: Answers the plain question almost word for word: no one is good enough; acceptance comes by believing in Jesus.
12. #11 The Witness of the Spirit, Discourse II (wesley-011-c0027): «accepted, not for any works of righteousness which he hath done, but by the mere, free mercy of God; wholly and solely for what the Son of God hath done and suffered for him.» Reason: God justifies the ungodly by free mercy, solely for Christ's sake, not for any goodness of ours.
13. #30 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 10 (wesley-030-c0066): «Faith, therefore, is still the root of all, of present as well as future salvation. Still we must say to every sinner, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved."» Reason: States that faith in Christ is the root of salvation, now and hereafter; the message to every sinner is believe.
14. #33 UPON OUR LORD'S SERMON ON THE MOUNT, Discourse 13 (wesley-033-c0042): «"Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but of his own mercy he saveth us." Learn to hang naked upon the cross of Christ, counting all thou hast done but dung and dross.» Reason: Counsel: stop resting on what you have done and trust wholly in Christ's cross, like the dying thief.
15. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0024): «Faith is the condition, and the only condition, of justification. It is the condition: none is justified but he that believes: without faith no man is justified. And it is the only condition» Reason: Answers 'how is a person saved': faith is the one and only condition of being justified before God.
16. #85 On Working out our own Salvation (wesley-085-c0016): «Afterwards we experience the proper Christian salvation; whereby, through grace, we "are saved by faith;" consisting of those two grand branches, justification and sanctification.» Reason: Explains what salvation by faith is: justification restores God's favour, sanctification restores his image.
17. #120 On the Wedding Garment (wesley-120-c0010): «It is through his merits alone that all believers are saved; that is, justified -- saved from the guilt, -- sanctified -- saved from the nature, of sin; and glorified -- taken into heaven.» Reason: Plain answer: believers are saved through Christ's merits alone, 'for the sake of Jesus Christ'.
18. #21 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 1 (wesley-021-c0055): «Whosoever thou art, to whom God hath given to be "poor in spirit," to feel thyself lost, thou hast a right thereto, through the gracious promise of Him who cannot lie. It is purchased for thee by the blood of the Lamb.» Reason: To one who feels lost and unworthy: heaven is purchased for you by Christ's blood, not earned.
19. #25 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 5 (wesley-025-c0042): «And we must all declare, "By grace ye are saved through faith; not of works, lest any man should boast." We must cry aloud to every penitent sinner, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved."» Reason: Wesley's summary of salvation by faith, not works, with the caveat that true faith works by love.
