1. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0002): «Wherewithal then shall a sinful man atone for any the least of his sins? With his own works? No. Were they ever so many or holy, they are not his own, but God's.» Reason: Answers 'I can never be good enough': our own works cannot atone for even the least sin.
2. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0003): «herein "God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died" to save us "By grace" then "are ye saved through faith." Grace is the source, faith the condition, of salvation.» Reason: Core summary: Christ died for us while sinners; we are saved by grace as source, faith as condition.
3. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0012): «Christian faith is then, not only an assent to the whole gospel of Christ, but also a full reliance on the blood of Christ; a trust in the merits of his life, death, and resurrection» Reason: Defines the saving faith: full reliance on Christ's blood and merits, not our own, as our salvation.
4. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0038): «True, to despair of being saved by their own works, their own merits, or righteousness. And so it ought; for none can trust in the merits of Christ, till he has utterly renounced his own.» Reason: Speaks to the despair of not being good enough: give up trusting your merits and trust Christ's.
5. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0040): «What! Mercy for all? For Zacchaeus, a public robber? For Mary Magdalene, a common harlot? Methinks I hear one say "Then I, even I, may hope for mercy!" And so thou mayest» Reason: Salvation by faith is comfort to self-condemned sinners: mercy is offered to all who call on him.
6. #3 Awake, Thou That Sleepest (wesley-003-c0035): «Alas! all this will never bring thee to God. It is in his account lighter than vanity. Dost thou know Jesus Christ, whom he hath sent? Hath he taught thee, that "by grace we are saved through faith» Reason: Moral goodness and reputation cannot bring us to God; salvation is by grace through faith, not works.
7. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0048): «there is no other way of obtaining a share in his merit than by faith in his name» Reason: States plainly that the only way to share in Christ's saving merit is faith in him; works without it profit nothing.
8. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0052): «suppose, I say, this sinner, helpless and hopeless, casts himself wholly on the mercy of God in Christ, (which indeed he cannot do but by the grace of God,) who can doubt but he is forgiven in that moment?» Reason: However lacking in good works, the sinner who casts himself on God's mercy in Christ is forgiven at once.
9. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0064): «Thou who feelest thou art just fit for hell, art just fit to advance his glory; the glory of his free grace, justifying the ungodly and him that worketh not. O come quickly! Believe in the Lord Jesus» Reason: Direct invitation to one who feels unworthy: God justifies the ungodly; believe and be reconciled to God.
10. #6 The Righteousness of Faith (wesley-006-c0049): «the only, means under heaven given to a man, whereby he may regain the favour of God, which is better than life itself, or the image of God, which is the true life of the soul, is the submitting to the "righteousness which is of faith,"» Reason: The only way to regain God's favour is to submit to the righteousness of faith by believing in Christ.
11. #6 The Righteousness of Faith (wesley-006-c0052): «Neither say in thy heart, "I cannot be accepted yet, because I am not good enough." Who is good enough -- who ever was -- to merit acceptance at God's hands?» Reason: Answers the plain question almost word for word: no one is good enough; acceptance comes by believing in Jesus.
12. #11 The Witness of the Spirit, Discourse II (wesley-011-c0027): «accepted, not for any works of righteousness which he hath done, but by the mere, free mercy of God; wholly and solely for what the Son of God hath done and suffered for him.» Reason: God justifies the ungodly by free mercy, solely for Christ's sake, not for any goodness of ours.
13. #30 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 10 (wesley-030-c0066): «Faith, therefore, is still the root of all, of present as well as future salvation. Still we must say to every sinner, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved."» Reason: States that faith in Christ is the root of salvation, now and hereafter; the message to every sinner is believe.
14. #33 UPON OUR LORD'S SERMON ON THE MOUNT, Discourse 13 (wesley-033-c0042): «"Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but of his own mercy he saveth us." Learn to hang naked upon the cross of Christ, counting all thou hast done but dung and dross.» Reason: Counsel: stop resting on what you have done and trust wholly in Christ's cross, like the dying thief.
15. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0024): «Faith is the condition, and the only condition, of justification. It is the condition: none is justified but he that believes: without faith no man is justified. And it is the only condition» Reason: Answers 'how is a person saved': faith is the one and only condition of being justified before God.
16. #85 On Working out our own Salvation (wesley-085-c0016): «Afterwards we experience the proper Christian salvation; whereby, through grace, we "are saved by faith;" consisting of those two grand branches, justification and sanctification.» Reason: Explains what salvation by faith is: justification restores God's favour, sanctification restores his image.
17. #120 On the Wedding Garment (wesley-120-c0010): «It is through his merits alone that all believers are saved; that is, justified -- saved from the guilt, -- sanctified -- saved from the nature, of sin; and glorified -- taken into heaven.» Reason: Plain answer: believers are saved through Christ's merits alone, 'for the sake of Jesus Christ'.
18. #21 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 1 (wesley-021-c0055): «Whosoever thou art, to whom God hath given to be "poor in spirit," to feel thyself lost, thou hast a right thereto, through the gracious promise of Him who cannot lie. It is purchased for thee by the blood of the Lamb.» Reason: To one who feels lost and unworthy: heaven is purchased for you by Christ's blood, not earned.
19. #25 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 5 (wesley-025-c0042): «And we must all declare, "By grace ye are saved through faith; not of works, lest any man should boast." We must cry aloud to every penitent sinner, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved."» Reason: Wesley's summary of salvation by faith, not works, with the caveat that true faith works by love.

column5: What does it mean to be justified? Does Wesley say God justifies good people or ungodly people?
column8:
#5 Justification By Faith, wesley-005-c0000: "«To him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.»" Romans 4:5. 1. How a sinner may be justified before God, the Lord and Judge of all, is a question of no common importance to every child of man. It contains the foundation of all our hope, inasmuch as while we are at enmity with God, there can be no true peace, no solid joy, either in time or in eternity. What peace can there be, while our own heart condemns us; and much more, He that is "greater than our heart, and knoweth all things?" What solid joy, either in this world or that to come, while "the wrath of God abideth on us?"
Already labelled grade 1 (unchanged): #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation: «Justification is another word for pardon. It is the forgiveness of all our sins; and , what is necessarily implied therein, our acceptance with God.»
column9:
1. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0015): «it is not the being made actually just and righteous. This is "sanctification;" which is, indeed, in some degree, the immediate fruit of justification, but, nevertheless, is a distinct gift of God» Reason: Explains what justification is not: being made righteous is sanctification; justification is what God does for us through his Son.
2. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0024): «His sins, all his past sins, in thought, word, and deed, are covered, are blotted out, shall not be remembered or mentioned against him, any more than if they had not been.» Reason: Defines justification as forgiveness: all past sins blotted out because Christ suffered for the sinner.
3. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0028): «And the Apostle tells us expressly, the ungodly: "He (that is, God) justifieth the ungodly;" the ungodly of every kind and degree; and none but the ungodly.» Reason: Answers directly: God justifies the ungodly of every kind and degree; only sinners need pardon.
4. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0033): «He saves from the guilt of sin, (and, at the same time, from the power,) sinners of every kind, of every degree: men who, till then, were altogether ungodly; in whom the love of the Father was not» Reason: Christ seeks and saves the lost, pardoning sinners of every kind and degree; direct answer to 'terrible things'.
5. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0041): «But on what terms, then, is he justified who is altogether "ungodly," and till that time "worketh not?" on one alone; which is faith» Reason: States the one condition on which the ungodly are justified: faith, without prior obedience to the law.
6. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0043): «And at what time soever a sinner thus believes, be it in early childhood, in the strength of his years, or when he is old and hoary-haired, God justifieth that ungodly one» Reason: Whenever a sinner trusts that Christ died for him, God pardons him though he had no good thing.
7. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0050): «so he counteth us righteous, from the time we believe in him: That is, he doth not punish us for our sins; yea, treats us as though we are guiltless and righteous.» Reason: Explains what being justified means: God does not punish our sins and treats us as righteous from the moment we believe.
8. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0052): «For suppose a sinner of any kind or degree, in a full sense of his total ungodliness, of his utter inability to think, speak, or do good, and his absolute meetness for hell-fire» Reason: Any sinner, however bad, who casts himself on God's mercy in Christ is forgiven in that moment.
9. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0062): «I charge thee before God, the Judge of all, go straight unto him, with all thy ungodliness. Take heed thou destroy not thy own soul by pleading thy righteousness, more or less.» Reason: Direct exhortation to the worst sinner: come to God as you are; he justifies the ungodly.
10. #6 The Righteousness of Faith (wesley-006-c0027): «If thou wert not ungodly, there would be no room for him to justify thee as ungodly. But now draw near, in fill assurance of faith.» Reason: Your ungodliness is exactly why God can justify you; only believe.
11. #6 The Righteousness of Faith (wesley-006-c0052): «Neither say in thy heart, "I cannot be accepted yet, because I am not good enough." Who is good enough -- who ever was -- to merit acceptance at God's hands?» Reason: No one is good enough to be accepted; acceptance comes by believing in Jesus, not by first becoming good.
12. #11 The Witness of the Spirit, Discourse II (wesley-011-c0027): «that God justifieth the ungodly? --him that, till the moment he is justified, is all ungodly, void of all true holiness» Reason: God justifies the ungodly by free mercy, for Christ's sake, not for any goodness in them.
13. #19 The Great Privilege of those that are Born of God (wesley-019-c0001): «Justification implies only a relative, the new birth a real, change. God in justifying us does something for us; in begetting us again, he does the work in us.» Reason: Clear definition: justification changes our relation to God, restoring his favour and taking away guilt.
14. #20 The Lord our Righteousness (wesley-020-c0026): «all believers are forgiven and accepted, not for the sake of anything in them, or of anything that ever was, that is, or ever can be done by them, but wholly and solely for the sake of what Christ hath done and suffered for them.» Reason: God accepts believers not for their goodness but wholly for Christ's sake.
15. #35 The Law Established through Faith, Discourse I (wesley-035-c0037): «We allow, (1.) That God justifies the ungodly; him that, till that hour, is totally ungodly; -- full of all evil, void of all good» Reason: Summarises the doctrine: God justifies the totally ungodly by faith alone, accepting them through Christ's merits.
16. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0024): «Faith is the condition, and the only condition, of justification. It is the condition: none is justified but he that believes: without faith no man is justified.» Reason: States how one is justified: by faith alone; every one who believes is justified, whatever else he has.
17. #53 On the Death of the Rev. Mr. George Whitefield (wesley-053-c0062): «Here then is the sole meritorious cause of every blessing we do or can enjoy; in particular of our pardon and acceptance with God, of our full and free justification.» Reason: Christ's death is the sole ground of our pardon and justification, received not by works but by faith alone.
18. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0041): «Whatsoever your sins be, "though red like crimson," though more than the hairs of your head, "return ye unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon you, and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon."» Reason: Direct promise for one who has done terrible things: whatever your sins, God will abundantly pardon.

column5: If we are saved by faith alone, do good works still matter? What did Wesley say about faith and works together?
column8: #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation, wesley-043-c0035: And there are so necessary, that if a man willingly neglect them, he cannot reasonably expect that he shall ever be sanctified; he cannot grow in grace, in the image of God, the mind which was in Christ Jesus; nay, he cannot retain the grace he has received; he cannot continue in faith, or in the favour of God. What is the inference we mist draw herefrom? Why, that both repentance, rightly understood, and «the practice of all good works, --works of piety, as well as works of mercy (now properly so called, since they spring from faith), are, in some sense, necessary to sanctification.» 6. I say, "repentance rightly understood"; for this must not be confounded with the former repentance.
column9:
1. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0026): «"It would be so, if we spake, as some do, of a faith which was separate from these; but we speak of a faith which is not so, but productive of all good works, and all holiness."» Reason: Answers the objection directly: saving faith is not against good works but produces all good works and holiness.
2. #5 Justification By Faith (wesley-005-c0037): «All truly "good works" (to use the words of our Church) "follow after justification;" and they are therefore good and "acceptable to God in Christ," because they "spring out of a true and living faith."» Reason: Explains the order: truly good works follow justification and spring from living faith.
3. #17 The Circumcision of the Heart (wesley-017-c0035): «Our gospel, as it knows no other foundation of good works than faith, or of faith than Christ» Reason: Faith in Christ is the only foundation of good works; Christ's Spirit inspires both our faith and our works.
4. #27 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 7 (wesley-027-c0003): «Some have magnified faith to the utter exclusion of good works, not only from being the cause of our justification, (for we know that man is justified freely by the redemption which is in Jesus,) but from being the necessary fruit of it» Reason: Names both errors: works are not the cause of justification, but they are its necessary fruit.
5. #33 UPON OUR LORD'S SERMON ON THE MOUNT, Discourse 13 (wesley-033-c0044): «That faith which hath not works, which doth not produce both inward and outward holiness, which does not stamp the whole image of God on the heart, and purify us as he is pure» Reason: Faith without works cannot save; true gospel faith always produces inward and outward holiness.
6. #35 The Law Established through Faith, Discourse I (wesley-035-c0032): «Whereas now all good works, though as necessary as ever, are not antecedent to our acceptance, but consequent upon it.» Reason: Good works are as necessary as ever, but they follow our acceptance by grace rather than earning it.
7. #35 The Law Established through Faith, Discourse I (wesley-035-c0035): «We are justified without the works of the law, as any previous condition of justification; but they are an immediate fruit of that faith whereby we are justified.» Reason: Wesley's balanced answer: justified by faith without works, yet if works do not follow, the faith is worthless.
8. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0027): «Not in the same degree; for those fruits are only necessary conditionally; if there be time and opportunity for them. otherwise a man may be justified without them, as was the thief upon the cross» Reason: Explains how works relate to justification: needed if there is opportunity, but faith alone is indispensable.
9. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0050): «for this repentance and these fruits are only remotely necessary, --necessary in order to the continuance of his faith, as well as the increase of it; whereas faith is immediately and directly necessary to sanctification.» Reason: Good works matter because they keep and increase faith, while faith alone is the direct condition.
10. #91 On Charity (wesley-091-c0050): «Yet if this faith does not work by love, if it does not produce universal holiness, if it does not bring forth lowliness, meekness, and resignation, it will profit me nothing.» Reason: Faith that does not work by love and produce holiness profits nothing; faith and works belong together.
11. #99 The Reward of the Righteous (wesley-099-c0017): «Good works are so far from being hindrances of our salvation; they are so far from being insignificant, from being of no account in Christianity; that, supposing them to spring from a right principle, they are the perfection of religion.» Reason: Rebuts the idea that works don't matter: springing from faith, good works are the height of religion.
12. #85 On Working out our own Salvation (wesley-085-c0037): «Secondly, God worketh in you; therefore you must work: You must be "workers together with him," (they are the very words of the Apostle,) otherwise he will cease working.» Reason: Because God works in believers, they must work with him; grace does not make our effort unnecessary.
13. #20 The Lord our Righteousness (wesley-020-c0041): «But do not you believe inherent righteousness? Yes, in its proper place; not as the ground of our acceptance with God, but as the fruit of it; not in the place of imputed righteousness, but as consequent upon it.» Reason: Holy living matters, but as the fruit of acceptance with God, not its ground; Christ's righteousness alone is the basis.
14. #116 Causes of the Inefficacy of Christianity (wesley-116-c0047): «I do, blessed be God, gain, and save, and give all I can. And so, I trust in God, I shall do, while the breath of God is in my nostrils. But what then? I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Jesus my Lord! Still, I give up every plea beside» Reason: Wesley insists on giving all you can, yet pleads none of his own works for salvation, only Christ.

9. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0050): «for this repentance and these fruits are only remotely necessary, --necessary in order to the continuance of his faith, as well as the increase of it; whereas faith is immediately and directly necessary to sanctification.» Reason: Good works matter because they keep and increase faith, while faith alone is the direct condition.
10. #91 On Charity (wesley-091-c0050): «Yet if this faith does not work by love, if it does not produce universal holiness, if it does not bring forth lowliness, meekness, and resignation, it will profit me nothing.» Reason: Faith that does not work by love and produce holiness profits nothing; faith and works belong together.
11. #99 The Reward of the Righteous (wesley-099-c0017): «Good works are so far from being hindrances of our salvation; they are so far from being insignificant, from being of no account in Christianity; that, supposing them to spring from a right principle, they are the perfection of religion.» Reason: Rebuts the idea that works don't matter: springing from faith, good works are the height of religion.
12. #85 On Working out our own Salvation (wesley-085-c0037): «Secondly, God worketh in you; therefore you must work: You must be "workers together with him," (they are the very words of the Apostle,) otherwise he will cease working.» Reason: Because God works in believers, they must work with him; grace does not make our effort unnecessary.
13. #20 The Lord our Righteousness (wesley-020-c0041): «But do not you believe inherent righteousness? Yes, in its proper place; not as the ground of our acceptance with God, but as the fruit of it; not in the place of imputed righteousness, but as consequent upon it.» Reason: Holy living matters, but as the fruit of acceptance with God, not its ground; Christ's righteousness alone is the basis.
14. #116 Causes of the Inefficacy of Christianity (wesley-116-c0047): «I do, blessed be God, gain, and save, and give all I can. And so, I trust in God, I shall do, while the breath of God is in my nostrils. But what then? I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Jesus my Lord! Still, I give up every plea beside» Reason: Wesley insists on giving all you can, yet pleads none of his own works for salvation, only Christ.

column5: What does it mean to be born again? What did Wesley preach about the new birth?
column8:
#45 The New Birth, wesley-045-c0000: "Ye must be born again." John 3:7. 1. «If any doctrines within the whole compass of Christianity may be properly termed fundamental, they are doubtless these two, -- the doctrine of justification, and that of the new birth: The former relating to that great work which God does for us, in forgiving our sins; the latter, to the great work which God does in us, in renewing our fallen nature.» In order of time, neither of these is before the other: in the moment we are justified by the grace of God, through the redemption that is in Jesus, we are also "born of the Spirit;" but in order of thinking, as it is termed, justification precedes the new birth.
Already labelled grade 1 (unchanged): #18 The Marks of the New Birth: «Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.»
column9:
1. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0037): «It is the change wrought in the whole soul by the almighty Spirit of God when it is "created anew in Christ Jesus;" when it is "renewed after the image of God, in righteousness and true holiness;" when the love of the world is changed into the love of God; pride into humility; passion into meekness» Reason: Wesley's own definition of the new birth and a list of exactly what changes inside a person.
2. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0016): «This, then, is the foundation of the new birth, -- the entire corruption of our nature. Hence it is, that, being born in sin, we must be "born again."» Reason: Answers why we must be born again: our nature is corrupted from birth, so the Spirit must renew it.
3. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0029): «But as soon as he is born of God, there is a total change in all these particulars. The "eyes of his understanding are opened;"» Reason: Describes the change at new birth: spiritual eyes and ears opened, hearing God say sins are forgiven.
4. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0032): «He feels, he is conscious of, a "peace which passeth all understanding." He many times feels such a joy in God as is "unspeakable, and full of glory." He feels "the love of God shed abroad in his heart» Reason: Names what the born-again person inwardly experiences: peace, joy, and God's love felt in the heart.
5. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0042): «It cannot commence in the soul till that change be wrought; till, by the power of the Highest overshadowing us, we are "brought from darkness to light, from the power of Satan unto God;" that is, till we are born again» Reason: Explains why the new birth is necessary: holiness, and so salvation, cannot begin without it.
6. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0052): «the one being an act of man, purifying the body; the other a change wrought by God in the soul: So that the former is just as distinguishable from the latter, as the soul from the body, or water from the Holy Ghost.» Reason: Wesley's teaching that baptism is not the new birth; the new birth is God's inward change of the soul.
7. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0058): «This is a part of sanctification, not the whole; it is the gate to it, the entrance into it. When we are born again, then our sanctification, our inward and outward holiness, begins» Reason: Explains new birth as the beginning of holiness, followed by gradual growth, like a child born then growing.
8. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0072): «Let this therefore, if you have not already experienced this inward work of God, be your continual prayer: "Lord, add this to all thy blessings, -- let me be born again!» Reason: Direct counsel to someone who needs the new birth: church-going cannot replace it, so pray for it.
9. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0008): «In that instant we are born again, born from above, born of the Spirit: there is a real as well as a relative change. We are inwardly renewed by the power of God.» Reason: Says new birth happens with justification and describes the real inward change: love replaces pride, anger, self-will.
10. #14 The Repentance of Believers (wesley-014-c0073): «We allow, that at the very moment of justification, we are born again: In that instant we experience that inward change from "darkness into marvellous light;" from the image of the brute and the devil, into the image of God» Reason: Describes the inward change at new birth, and notes it is real but not yet complete holiness.
11. #83 On Patience (wesley-083-c0016): «And there is as great a change wrought in our souls when we are born of the Spirit, as was wrought in our bodies when we are born of a woman. There is, in that hour, a general change from inward sinfulness, to inward holiness.» Reason: Plainly states what changes when one is born of the Spirit: loves, desires, and will turned toward God.
12. #107 On God's Vineyard (wesley-107-c0015): «Not an outward change only, as from drunkenness to sobriety, from robbery or theft to honesty; (this is the poor, dry, miserable conceit of those that know nothing of real religion;) but an inward change from all unholy, to all holy tempers» Reason: Explains the new birth as an inward change of tempers, not mere outward reform; directly answers what changes.
13. #125 On Living Without God (wesley-125-c0022): «not, on the one hand, to despise the day of small things; nor, on the other, to mistake any of these partial changes for that entire, general change, the new birth» Reason: Distinguishes the new birth, a total inward change, from partial reforms people mistake for it.
14. #19 The Great Privilege of those that are Born of God (wesley-019-c0016): «But when he is born of God, born of the Spirit, how is the manner of his existence changed! His whole soul is now sensible of God» Reason: Describes how life changes when born of God: the soul senses God and lives by faith, love, prayer, praise.
15. #1 Salvation by Faith (wesley-001-c0025): «So that he who is thus justified, or saved by faith, is indeed born again. he is born again of the Spirit unto a new life, which "is hid with Christ in God."» Reason: Says the one saved by faith is born again to a new life and then grows from grace to grace.
16. #18 The Marks of the New Birth (wesley-018-c0045): «It is so to believe in God through Christ as not to commit sin and to enjoy at all times and in all places that peace of God which passeth all understanding» Reason: Wesley's summary of the marks of one born of the Spirit: faith, peace, hope, the Spirit's witness, love.
17. #18 The Marks of the New Birth (wesley-018-c0009): «An immediate and constant fruit of this faith whereby we are born of God, a fruit which can in no wise be separated from it, no, not for an hour, is power over sin» Reason: Names a key change in the born-again person: power over outward and inward sin.

column5: I am a Christian and I still struggle with pride and unbelief. Did Wesley say that sin remains in believers?
column8: #13 On Sin in Believers, wesley-013-c0062: Now, if you allow men may be justified while they have pride, anger, or unbelief in them; nay, if you aver, these are (at least for a time) in all that are justified; what wonder that we have so many proud, angry, unbelieving believers! «I do not suppose any man who is justified is a slave to sin: Yet I do suppose sin remains (at least for a time) in all that are justified.» "But, if sin remains in a believer, he is a sinful man: If pride, for instance, then he is proud; if self-will, then he is self-willed; if unbelief, then he is an unbeliever; consequently, no believer at all.
column9:
1. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0025): «They are daily sensible of sin remaining in their heart, -- pride, self-will, unbelief; and of sin cleaving to all they speak and do» Reason: Believers feel pride and unbelief yet are assured they are God's children; Christ dwells where sin remains.
2. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0030): «one says, "I felt anger to-day." Must I reply, "Then you have no faith?"» Reason: Rejects telling a struggling believer he has no faith; such a doctrine wounds and disarms weak believers.
3. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0045): «Every babe in Christ is holy, and yet not altogether so. He is saved from sin; yet not entirely: It remains, though it does not reign.» Reason: Direct doctrinal answer: sin remains in believers though it does not reign.
4. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0055): «A man may have pride in him, may think of himself in some particulars above what he ought to think, (and so be proud in that particular,) and yet not be a proud man in his general character.» Reason: Speaks to pride specifically: a believer may feel pride without being a proud man ruled by it.
5. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0058): «Resentment of an affront is sin; it is anomia, disconformity to the law of love. This has existed in me a thousand times. Yet it did not, and does not, reign.» Reason: Wesley's own experience: inward sin felt but not yielded to brings no condemnation.
6. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0064): «"But how can unbelief be in a believer?" That word has two meanings. It means either no faith, or little faith; either the absence of faith or the weakness of it.» Reason: Answers the doubting part: believers may have weak faith mixed with doubt without lacking faith.
7. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0066): «A man may be in God's favour though he feel sin; but not if he yields to it. Having sin does not forfeit the favour of God; giving way to sin does.» Reason: Reassures that feeling sin does not mean loss of salvation; only yielding to it does.
8. #8 THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE SPIRIT (wesley-008-c0021): «They are not condemned, thirdly, for inward sin, even though it does now remain. That the corruption of nature does still remain, even in those who are the children of God by faith» Reason: Says believers are not condemned for remaining inward sin like pride; it is daily experience.
9. #8 THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE SPIRIT (wesley-008-c0050): «Then fret not thyself because of ungodliness, though it still remain in thy heart. Repine not, because thou still comest short of the glorious image of God; nor yet because pride, self-will, or unbelief, cleave to all thy words and works.» Reason: Direct comfort to believers troubled by remaining pride and unbelief: no condemnation, do not fret.
10. #14 The Repentance of Believers (wesley-014-c0007): «it does not reign, but it does remain. And a conviction of the sin which remains in our heart, is one great branch of the repentance we are now speaking of.» Reason: Believers soon feel pride still in their hearts yet know they are in God's favour.
11. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0011): «yet they feel in themselves sometimes pride or self-will, sometimes anger or unbelief. They find one or more of these frequently stirring in their heart, though not conquering» Reason: Describes the normal believer's experience of pride and unbelief stirring while still a child of God.
12. #43 The Scripture Way of Salvation (wesley-043-c0037): «It is properly a conviction, wrought by the Holy Ghost, of the sin which still remains in our heart; of the phronema sarkos, the carnal mind, which "does still remain" (as our Church speaks) "even in them that are regenerate";» Reason: Says sin remains in the regenerate, and recognizing it does not imply doubting God's favour.
13. #82 On Temptation (wesley-082-c0022): «For even good men, in general, though sin has not dominion over the, yet are not freed from the remains of it. They have still the remains of an evil heart» Reason: Plainly states good men keep remains of sin, including pride, though sin has no dominion.
14. #123 The Deceitfulness of the Human Heart (wesley-123-c0030): «Only let it be remembered, that the heart, even of a believer, is not wholly purified when he is justified. Sin is then overcome, but it is not rooted out; it is conquered, but not destroyed.» Reason: Pride and self-will remain in the believer's heart after justification but cannot prevail while he watches and prays.
15. #83 On Patience (wesley-083-c0021): «The faith of a babe in Christ is weak, generally mingled with doubts or fears; with doubts, whether he has not deceived himself; or fear, that he shall not endure to the end.» Reason: Explains that doubting one's salvation is common in young believers' weak faith.
16. #72 Of Evil Angels (wesley-072-c0053): «If he inject doubts whether you are a child of God, or fears lest you should not endure to the end; "take to you for a helmet the hope of salvation."» Reason: Counsel for believers tempted to doubt they are God's children: hold fast the hope of salvation.

column5: Are people basically good? What did Wesley teach about original sin and the human heart?
column8: #44 Original Sin, wesley-044-c0000: "And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that «every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.»" Gen. 6:5. 1. How widely different is this from the fair pictures of human nature which men have drawn in all ages! The writings of many of the ancients abound with gay descriptions of the dignity of man; whom some of them paint as having all virtue and happiness in his composition, or, at least, entirely in his power, without being beholden to any other being; yea, as self-sufficient, able to live on his own stock, and little inferior to God himself. 2.
column9:
1. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0005): «The Scripture avers, that "by one man's disobedience all men were constituted sinners;" that "in Adam all died," spiritually died, lost the life and the image of God; that fallen, sinful Adam then "begat a son in his own likeness;"» Reason: Says from Scripture that all are sinners by nature from birth through Adam, against flattering views of human nature.
2. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0013): «But was there not good mingled with the evil? Was there not light intermixed with the darkness? No; none at all: "God saw that the whole imagination of the heart of man was only evil."» Reason: Directly answers whether natural man has good mixed in: none, apart from God's grace.
3. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0018): «From all these we learn, concerning man in his natural state, unassisted by the grace of God, that "every imagination of the thoughts of his heart is" still "evil, only evil," and that "continually."» Reason: Says people today are the same: natural man without grace is wholly evil, confirmed by experience.
4. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0024): «Were two infants in like manner to be brought up from the womb without being instructed in any religion, there is little room to doubt but (unless the grace of God interposed) the event would be just the same.» Reason: Answers 'from the start': untaught infants would have no knowledge or love of God by nature.
5. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0031): «Therefore all pride is idolatry; it is ascribing to ourselves what is due to God alone. And although pride was not made for man, yet where is the man that is born without it?» Reason: Pride is inborn, not learned: no one is born without it.
6. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0047): «The other declares that all men are conceived in sin," and "shapen in wickedness;" -- that hence there is in every man a "carnal mind, which is enmity against God,» Reason: Contrasts the view that natural good outweighs evil with Christianity's teaching that all are conceived in sin.
7. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0050): «But here is the shibboleth: Is man by nature filled with all manner of evil? Is he void of all good? Is he wholly fallen? Is his soul totally corrupted?» Reason: States the decisive test: human nature is wholly fallen, not merely flawed by some vices.
8. #44 Original Sin (wesley-044-c0059): «Know your disease! Know your cure! Ye were born in sin: Therefore, "ye must be born again," born of God. By nature ye are wholly corrupted. 9. #45 The New Birth (wesley-045-c0015): «The natural consequence of this is, that every one descended from him comes into the world spiritually dead, dead to God, wholly dead in sin; entirely void of the life of God» Reason: Explains that everyone is born spiritually dead and corrupted through Adam's fall, hence the need of new birth.
10. #95 On the Education of Children (wesley-095-c0013): «What those spiritual diseases which every one that is born of a woman brings with him into the world? Is not the first of the Atheism?» Reason: Names the spiritual diseases every person brings into the world at birth, not picked up later.
11. #123 The Deceitfulness of the Human Heart (wesley-123-c0018): «However therefore men may differ in their outward ways, (in which, undoubtedly, there are a thousand differences,) yet in the inward root, the enmity against God, Atheism, pride, self-will, and idolatry, it is true of all» Reason: Outward behaviour differs, but the inward root of sin is in every natural heart.
12. #53 On the Death of the Rev. Mr. George Whitefield (wesley-053-c0060): «For it is not enough to say, all men are sick of sin: no, we are all "dead in trespasses and sins." It follows, that all the children of men are, "by nature, children of wrath."» Reason: States the early Methodist teaching: no natural power to do good; all are dead in sin by nature.
13. #13 On Sin in Believers (wesley-013-c0002): «"Original sin is the corruption of the nature of every man, whereby man is in his own nature inclined to evil, so that the flesh lusteth contrary to the Spirit.» Reason: Gives the Church's definition of original sin that Wesley endorses: every person's nature is inclined to evil.

column5: How should I treat Christians who disagree with me on doctrine? What did Wesley mean by a catholic spirit?
column8: #39 Catholic Spirit, wesley-039-c0054: III. 1. One inference we may make from what has been said. We may learn from hence, what is a catholic spirit. There is scarce any expression which has been more grossly misunderstood, and more dangerously misapplied, than this: but it will be easy for any who calmly consider the preceding observations, to correct any such misapprehensions of it, and to prevent any such misapplication. For, from hence we may learn, first, that «a catholic spirit is not speculative latitudinarianism. It is not an indifference to all opinions: this is the spawn of hell, not the offspring of heaven.» This unsettledness of thought, this being "driven to and fro, and tossed about with every wind of doctrine," is a great curse, not a blessing, an irreconcilable enemy, not a friend, to true catholicism.
column9:
1. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0005): «But although a difference in opinions or modes of worship may prevent an entire external union, yet need it prevent our union in affection? Though we cannot think alike, may we not love alike? May we not be of one heart, though we are not of one opinion? Without all doubt, we may.» Reason: Direct answer: Christians who differ in opinion and worship can still be united in love and good works.
2. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0016): «Every wise man, therefore, will allow others the same liberty of thinking which he desires they should allow him; and will no more insist on their embracing his opinions, than he would have them to insist on his embracing theirs.» Reason: Counsel to grant others the same freedom of judgment you want, and bear with those who differ.
3. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0021): «God has given no right to any of the children of men thus to lord it over the conscience of his brethren; but every man must judge for himself, as every man must give an account of himself to God.» Reason: Explains why we must not force our views on others: each answers to God by his own conscience.
4. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0026): «Let all these things stand by: we will talk of them, if need be, at a more convenient season, my only question at present is this, "Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart?"» Reason: Wesley sets aside church order and sacrament disputes; the one test for fellowship is a heart right with God.
5. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0039): «Keep you your opinion; I mine; and that as steadily as ever. You need not even endeavour to come over to me, or bring me over to you.» Reason: Shows how to unite without pretending: both keep their convictions firmly yet join hands in love.
6. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0043): «then love me with a very tender affection, as a friend that is closer than a brother; as a brother in Christ, a fellow citizen of the New Jerusalem, a fellow soldier engaged in the same warfare» Reason: Says those who differ but whose hearts are right should be close friends and brothers in Christ.
7. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0045): «Love me so as to think no evil of me; to put away all jealousy and evil-surmising.» Reason: Practical counsel on treating a fellow Christian who differs: patient love, no suspicion, best construction on their actions.
8. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0046): «commend me to God in all thy prayers; wrestle with him in my behalf, that he would speedily correct what he sees amiss, and supply what is wanting in me.» Reason: Another concrete duty toward a differing Christian: pray earnestly for one another.
9. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0050): «So far as in conscience thou canst (retaining still thy own opinions, and thy own manner of worshipping God), join with me in the work of God; and let us go on hand in hand.» Reason: Directly answers whether we can work together: yes, each keeping his own opinions and worship.
10. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0062): «But while he is steadily fixed in his religious principles in what he believes to be the truth as it is in Jesus; while he firmly adheres to that worship of God which he judges to be most acceptable in his sight» Reason: Defines a catholic spirit: firm in one's own beliefs and church, yet loving all; catholic love is a catholic spirit.
11. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0065): «loves as friends as brethren in the Lord as members of Christ and children of God as joint partakers now of the present kingdom of God and fellow heirs of his eternal kingdom all of whatever opinion or worship or congregation who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ» Reason: Wesley's fullest definition of the man of catholic spirit: keeps his own blessings, loves all believers as brethren.
12. #39 Catholic Spirit (wesley-039-c0067): «Take heed, lest thou be either wavering in thy judgement, or straitened in thy bowels: but keep an even pace, rooted in the faith once delivered to the saints, and grounded in love» Reason: Closing exhortation: avoid both wavering convictions and narrow affections; be rooted in faith and grounded in love.
13. #53 On the Death of the Rev. Mr. George Whitefield (wesley-053-c0058): «There are many doctrines of a less essential nature, with regard to which even the sincere children of God (such is the present weakness of human understanding) are and have been divided for many ages. In these we may think and let think; we may "agree to disagree."» Reason: Counsel to agree to disagree on lesser doctrines while holding fast the essentials of the faith.
14. #53 On the Death of the Rev. Mr. George Whitefield (wesley-053-c0072): «One who loves as friends, as brethren in the Lord, as joint partakers of the present kingdom of heaven, and fellow heirs of His eternal kingdom, all, of whatever opinion, mode of worship, or congregation, who believe in the Lord Jesus» Reason: Answers who is the man of a catholic spirit: he loves, prays for, and helps believers of every persuasion.
15. #53 On the Death of the Rev. Mr. George Whitefield (wesley-053-c0076): «Go and learn that truly catholic love which "is not rash," or hasty in judging; that love which "thinks no evil;" which "believes and hopes all things;" which makes all the allowances for others that we desire others should make for us!» Reason: Exhorts to catholic love that judges slowly and sees God's grace in others whatever their opinion or worship.
16. #20 The Lord our Righteousness (wesley-020-c0009): «I say seem; because I am throughly convinced, that many of them only seem to differ. The disagreement is more in words than in sentiments: They are much nearer in judgment than in language.» Reason: Points out that many doctrinal disagreements among believers are more in words than in substance.
17. #20 The Lord our Righteousness (wesley-020-c0022): «How then can we be rigorous in requiring others to use just the same expressions with us? 3. We may go a step farther yet: Men may differ from us in their opinions, as well as their expressions, and nevertheless be partakers with us of the same precious faith.» Reason: Says those who differ in expression or even opinion may share the same saving faith; don't demand uniformity.
18. #20 The Lord our Righteousness (wesley-020-c0065): «Bear with me, as I do with you; else how shall we "fulfil the law of Christ?"» Reason: Wesley's own plea to a doctrinal opponent: bear with each other, same foundation, no coldness or unkindness.
19. #38 A Caution against Bigotry (wesley-038-c0072): «If he forbid you, do not you forbid him. Rather labour, and watch, and pray the more, to confirm your love toward him. If he speak all manner of evil of you, speak all manner of good (that is true) of him.» Reason: Counsel for when a Christian of another party opposes you: do not retaliate, increase your love and speak well.
20. #38 A Caution against Bigotry (wesley-038-c0066): «Do I not discourage him, because he is not of my Church, by disputing with him concerning it, by raising objections, and by perplexing his mind with distant consequences?» Reason: Self-examination questions on how we treat Christians of another church; names bigotry in word and action.
21. #74 Of the Church (wesley-074-c0030): «Whoever they are that have one Spirit one hope one Lord one faith one God and Father of all I can easily bear with their holding wrong opinions yea and superstitious modes of worship» Reason: Wesley bears with those holding wrong opinions if they share one Spirit, Lord, and faith.
22. #115 The Ministerial Office (wesley-115-c0039): «receiving all that love God in every Church as our brother, and sister, and mother. And in order to their union with us we require no unity in opinions, or in modes of worship» Reason: States his practice: receive God-lovers of every church as family, requiring no agreement in opinions or worship.

column5: I used to believe and then I fell away. What did Wesley say to backsliders who think God will not take them back?
column8: #86 A Call to Backsliders, wesley-086-c0007: And yet we need not utterly give up even these. We have known some even of the careless ones whom God has visited again, and restored to their first love. «But we may have much more hope for those backsliders who are not careless, who are still uneasy; -- those who fain would escape out of the snare of the devil, but think it is impossible.» They are fully convinced they cannot save themselves, and believe God will not save them. They believe he has irrevocably "shut up his lovingkindness in displeasure." They fortify themselves in believing this, by abundance of reasons; and unless those reasons are clearly removed, they cannot hope for any deliverance.
column9:
1. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0030): «Yea, he will; not until seven times only, or until seventy times seven. Nay, were your rebellions multiplied as the stars of heaven; were they more in number than the hairs of your head; yet "return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon you; and to our God, and he will abundantly pardon."» Reason: Direct answer: unlike an earthly king, God pardons again, however many times one has rebelled; return and he will pardon.
2. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0048): «Whatever other passages of Scripture may condemn you, it is certain, you are not condemned either by the sixth or the tenth of the Hebrews.» Reason: Answers the fear that Hebrews 6 and 10 shut out the fallen; shows those texts do not apply to most backsliders.
3. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0054): «Bad as you are, you shudder at the thought: there fore that sacrifice still remains for you. Come then, cast away your needless fears! "Come boldly to the throne of grace." The way is still open.» Reason: Tells the fearful backslider Christ's sacrifice still remains for them; the way back is open.
4. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0063): «How marvellously then have you been afraid, where no fear is! Dismiss that vain terror; let your fear be more rational for the time to come.» Reason: Removes the fear of having committed the unpardonable sin, a common reason backsliders think God won't take them back.
5. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0036): «But observe! This has no reference to eternal death. It does by no means imply that you are condemned to die the second death. No; it rather implies the contrary: The body is destroyed, that the soul may escape destruction.» Reason: Answers the fear of a 'sin unto death': it does not mean eternal damnation for the backslider.
6. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0067): «Innumerable are the instances of this kind, of those who had fallen, but now stand upright. Indeed, it is so far from being an uncommon thing for a believer to fall and be restored» Reason: From experience: countless fallen believers have been restored; falling and returning is common, not hopeless.
7. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0071): «many who had fallen either from justifying or from sanctifying grace, and so deeply fallen that they could hardly be ranked among the servants of God, have been restored» Reason: Even the deeply fallen have been restored to all they lost, often in an instant; strong hope for the returning.
8. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0074): «but for those who feel "the remembrance of their sins is grievous unto them, the burden of them intolerable." We set before these an open door of hope: Let them go in and give thanks unto the Lord» Reason: Wesley's closing word to grieving backsliders: an open door of hope; God is gracious and will remove their sins.
9. #68 The Wisdom of God's Counsels (wesley-068-c0063): «Surely He is able to heal all their backslidings: For with God no word is impossible. And is he not willing too? He is "God, and not man; therefore his compassions fail not." Let no backslider despair.» Reason: Says God is both able and willing to heal backsliding; no backslider should despair but return.
10. #24 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 4 (wesley-024-c0034): «A believer may fall, and not fall away. He may fall and rise again. And if he should fall, even into sin, yet this case, dreadful as it is, is not desperate.» Reason: Distinguishes falling from total apostasy: one who falls may rise again, for Christ is our Advocate.
11. #8 THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE SPIRIT (wesley-008-c0049): «Come unto him as at first, as wretched and poor, as sinful, miserable, blind and naked! And beware thou suffer thy soul to take no rest, till his pardoning love be again revealed; till he "heal thy backslidings,"» Reason: Direct counsel to one who has fallen back into sin: come to God again as at first until he heals your backsliding.

column5: I walked away from God years ago. I want to come back, but I'm scared he won't have me. Is it too late?
column6: I used to believe and then I fell away. What did Wesley say to backsliders who think God will not take them back?
column8: #86 A Call to Backsliders, wesley-086-c0007: And yet we need not utterly give up even these. We have known some even of the careless ones whom God has visited again, and restored to their first love. «But we may have much more hope for those backsliders who are not careless, who are still uneasy; -- those who fain would escape out of the snare of the devil, but think it is impossible.» They are fully convinced they cannot save themselves, and believe God will not save them. They believe he has irrevocably "shut up his lovingkindness in displeasure." They fortify themselves in believing this, by abundance of reasons; and unless those reasons are clearly removed, they cannot hope for any deliverance.
column9:
1. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0030): «Yea, he will; not until seven times only, or until seventy times seven. Nay, were your rebellions multiplied as the stars of heaven; were they more in number than the hairs of your head; yet "return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon you; and to our God, and he will abundantly pardon."» Reason: Direct answer: unlike an earthly king, God pardons again, however many times one has rebelled; return and he will pardon.
2. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0048): «Whatever other passages of Scripture may condemn you, it is certain, you are not condemned either by the sixth or the tenth of the Hebrews.» Reason: Answers the fear that Hebrews 6 and 10 shut out the fallen; shows those texts do not apply to most backsliders.
3. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0054): «Bad as you are, you shudder at the thought: there fore that sacrifice still remains for you. Come then, cast away your needless fears! "Come boldly to the throne of grace." The way is still open.» Reason: Tells the fearful backslider Christ's sacrifice still remains for them; the way back is open.
4. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0063): «How marvellously then have you been afraid, where no fear is! Dismiss that vain terror; let your fear be more rational for the time to come.» Reason: Removes the fear of having committed the unpardonable sin, a common reason backsliders think God won't take them back.
5. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0036): «But observe! This has no reference to eternal death. It does by no means imply that you are condemned to die the second death. No; it rather implies the contrary: The body is destroyed, that the soul may escape destruction.» Reason: Answers the fear of a 'sin unto death': it does not mean eternal damnation for the backslider.
6. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0067): «Innumerable are the instances of this kind, of those who had fallen, but now stand upright. Indeed, it is so far from being an uncommon thing for a believer to fall and be restored» Reason: From experience: countless fallen believers have been restored; falling and returning is common, not hopeless.
7. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0071): «many who had fallen either from justifying or from sanctifying grace, and so deeply fallen that they could hardly be ranked among the servants of God, have been restored» Reason: Even the deeply fallen have been restored to all they lost, often in an instant; strong hope for the returning.
8. #86 A Call to Backsliders (wesley-086-c0074): «but for those who feel "the remembrance of their sins is grievous unto them, the burden of them intolerable." We set before these an open door of hope: Let them go in and give thanks unto the Lord» Reason: Wesley's closing word to grieving backsliders: an open door of hope; God is gracious and will remove their sins.
9. #68 The Wisdom of God's Counsels (wesley-068-c0063): «Surely He is able to heal all their backslidings: For with God no word is impossible. And is he not willing too? He is "God, and not man; therefore his compassions fail not." Let no backslider despair.» Reason: Says God is both able and willing to heal backsliding; no backslider should despair but return.
10. #24 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 4 (wesley-024-c0034): «A believer may fall, and not fall away. He may fall and rise again. And if he should fall, even into sin, yet this case, dreadful as it is, is not desperate.» Reason: Distinguishes falling from total apostasy: one who falls may rise again, for Christ is our Advocate.
11. #8 THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE SPIRIT (wesley-008-c0049): «Come unto him as at first, as wretched and poor, as sinful, miserable, blind and naked! And beware thou suffer thy soul to take no rest, till his pardoning love be again revealed; till he "heal thy backslidings,"» Reason: Direct counsel to one who has fallen back into sin: come to God again as at first until he heals your backsliding.

column5: What does it mean to deny yourself and take up your cross? What did Wesley say about self-denial?
column8: #48 Self-denial, wesley-048-c0002: It no more regards any particular order of men, or particular time, than any particular country. No: It is of the most universal nature, respecting all times, and all persons, yea, and all things; not meats and drinks only, and things pertaining to the senses. The meaning is, "If any man," of whatever rank, station, circumstances, in any nation, in any age of the world, "will" effectually "come after me, let him deny himself" in all things; let him "take up his cross" of whatever kind; yea, and that "daily; and follow me." 2. «The denying ourselves and the taking up our cross, in the full extent of the expression, is not a thing of small concern: It is not expedient only, as are some of the circumstantials of religion; but it is absolutely, indispensably necessary, either to our becoming or continuing his disciples.»
column9:
1. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0022): «We see the nature of self-denial: It is the denying or refusing to follow ours own will, from a conviction that the will of God is the only rule of action to us.» Reason: Wesley's definition of self-denial and its ground: refusing our own will because God's will is our only rule.
2. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0025): «He cannot, at one and the same time, follow his own will, and follow the will of God: He must choose the one or the other; denying God's will, to follow his own; or denying himself, to follow the will of God.» Reason: Explains why self-denial is unavoidable: our will and God's now run in opposite directions, so we must choose.
3. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0028): «to deny ourselves, is, to deny our own will, where it does not fall in with the will of God; and that however pleasing it may be. It is, to deny ourselves any pleasure which does not spring from, and lead to, God» Reason: Answers how much to give up: any pleasure or wish not in line with God's will; also defines the cross.
4. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0031): «it is often needful to pluck out, as it were, a right eye, to cut off a right hand; -- so painful is either the thing itself which must be done, or the only means of doing it; the parting, suppose, with a foolish desire, with an inordinate affection» Reason: Says following Christ may mean painfully parting with a cherished desire or attachment, to heal the soul.
5. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0034): «So when our Lord said to the rich young man, "Go, sell that thou hast, and give it to the poor," (as well knowing, this was the only means of healing his covetousness,) the very thought of it gave him so much pain, that "he went away sorrowful;"» Reason: Uses the rich young ruler to show a cross Christ may ask: giving up what we cling to.
6. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0036): «we do not properly "take up our cross," but when we voluntarily suffer what it is in our power to avoid; when we willingly embrace the will of God, though contrary to our own» Reason: Explains what taking up the cross means, as distinct from bearing what is imposed: freely embracing God's will.
7. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0039): «In all this, we may easily conceive our blessed Lord to act as the Physician of our souls, not merely "for his own pleasure, but for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness."» Reason: Reassures that the cross God gives is measured for our good, like a physician causing pain only to heal.
8. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0041): «It does not imply the disciplining ourselves; (as some speak;) the literally tearing our own flesh: the wearing hair-cloth, or iron-girdles, or anything else that would impair our bodily health» Reason: Clarifies what self-denial is not (self-torment) and what it is: embracing God's will even when painful.
9. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0043): «But where none of these is wanting, the great hindrance of our receiving or growing in the grace of God is always the want of denying ourselves, or taking up our cross.» Reason: Explains why self-denial matters: lack of it is always the main hindrance to receiving or growing in grace.
10. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0064): «Delay not the time, but practise it immediately, from this very hour! Practise it universally, on every one of the thousand occasions which will occur in all circumstances of life! Practise it daily» Reason: Direct exhortation on how to practise self-denial: now, in everyday particulars, daily, asking God for strength.
11. #108 On Riches (wesley-108-c0041): «unless a man do "deny himself" every pleasure which does not prepare him for taking pleasure in God, "and take up his cross daily,"--obey every command of God, however grievous to flesh and blood,--he cannot be a disciple of Christ» Reason: States the measure of self-denial: give up any pleasure that doesn't lead to delight in God; obey even when hard.
12. #105 On Conscience (wesley-105-c0038): «What God forbids may be pleasing to our evil nature: There you are called to deny yourself, or you deny your Master. What he enjoins may be painful to nature: There take up your cross.» Reason: Plain rule for daily life: refuse what God forbids though pleasant, do what he commands though painful.

column5: My mind wanders when I try to pray. Are wandering thoughts a sin? What did Wesley say?
column8: #41 Wandering Thoughts, wesley-041-c0003: In order to do this in some degree, I purpose to inquire, I. What are the several sorts of wandering thoughts? II. What are the general occasions of them? III. Which of them are sinful, and which not? IV. Which of them we may expect and pray to be delivered from? I. 1. I purpose to inquire, First, What are the several sorts of wandering thoughts? The particular sorts are innumerable; but, in general, they are of two sorts: «Thoughts that wander from God; and thoughts that wander from the particular point we have in hand.» 2.
column9:
1. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0018): «The imagination, without leave, starts to and fro, and carries us away hither and thither, whether we will or no; and all this from the merely natural motion of the spirits, or vibration of the nerves.» Reason: Explains the cause: the mind drifts involuntarily from the body's natural workings, even in health.
2. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0024): «And, First, all those thoughts which wander from God, which leave him no room in our minds, are undoubtedly sinful.» Reason: Answers which wandering thoughts are sinful: those that wander from God himself, not mere distraction.
3. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0028): «however innocent they may be in themselves, do nevertheless become sinful, when they either produce or cherish and increase in us any sinful temper» Reason: Distinguishes when innocent distractions become sin: only when they feed a wrong desire or temper.
4. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0030): «wandering thoughts, in the latter sense of the word, that is, thoughts wherein our understanding wanders from the point it has in view, are no more sinful than the motion of the blood in our veins» Reason: Direct answer: a mind drifting off the point is no more sinful than blood moving in the veins.
5. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0032): «For it is no more a sin to understand what I see and hear, and in many cases cannot help seeing, hearing, and understanding, than it is to have eyes and ears.» Reason: Distractions from what we see and hear, or even thoughts the devil injects, are troublesome but not sinful.
6. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0034): «It follows that none of these wandering thoughts (whatever unwary persons have affirmed, thereby grieving whom the Lord had not grieved) are inconsistent with perfect love.» Reason: Reassures the worried: involuntary wandering thoughts do not contradict loving God fully; God is not grieved by them.
7. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0037): «those wherein the heart wanders from God; from all that are contrary to his will, or that leave us without God in the world; every one that is perfected in love is unquestionably delivered.» Reason: Says we may expect and pray for deliverance from the sinful kind of wandering thoughts.
8. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0039): «But the causes or occasions of these will remain as long as we remain in the body. So long, therefore, we have all reason to believe the effects will remain also.» Reason: Realistic counsel: ordinary distraction will last as long as we live in the body, so do not expect it to vanish.
9. #41 Wandering Thoughts (wesley-041-c0048): «Rather let us pray both with the spirit and with the understanding that all these things may work together for our good that we may suffer all the infirmities of our nature all the interruptions of men» Reason: Tells the asker how to respond: pray that distractions work for good and seek deliverance from sin, not from infirmity.

column5: I used to feel close to God, and now everything feels dark. What did Wesley say about the wilderness state?
column8: #46 The Wilderness State, wesley-046-c0001: In like manner, after God has delivered them that fear him from the bondage of sin and Satan; after they are "justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Jesus," yet not many of them immediately enter into "the rest which remaineth for the people of God." The greater part of them wander, more or less, out of the good way into which he hath brought them. They come, as it were, into a "waste and howling desert," where they are variously tempted and tormented: And this, «some, in allusion to the case of the Israelites, have termed "a wilderness state."» 2. Certain it is, that the condition wherein these are has a right the tenderest compassion.
column9:
1. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0004): «It properly consists in the loss of that faith which God once wrought in their heart. They that are in the wilderness, have not now that divine "evidence," that satisfactory conviction "of things not seen," which they once enjoyed.» Reason: Defines the wilderness state: loss of the clear faith and sense of God the believer once had.
2. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0011): «In consequence of the loss of faith and love, follows, Thirdly, loss of joy in the Holy Ghost. For if the loving consciousness of pardon be no more, the joy resulting therefrom cannot remain.» Reason: Explains why the former joy has gone: it flowed from a faith and witness that have weakened.
3. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0013): «That sweet tranquillity of mind, that composure of spirit, is gone. Painful doubt returns; doubt, whether we ever did, and perhaps whether we ever shall, believe.» Reason: Describes the lost peace and the doubts about whether one ever truly believed, a symptom the asker may feel.
4. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0019): «Therefore he never deserts us, as some speak; it is we only that desert him. (I.) 2. The most usual cause of inward darkness is sin, of one kind or another.» Reason: Answers 'what happened': God does not arbitrarily withdraw; darkness most often comes from sin.
5. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0024): «If therefore we are negligent of this, if we suffer business, company, or any avocation whatever, to prevent these secret exercises of the soul» Reason: Names neglect of private prayer as a common cause of the soul's life gradually dying away.
6. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0032): «And if we will not hear his warning voice, and return to him with our whole soul, we continue to grieve him with our idols, and running after other gods, we shall soon be cold, barren, and dry» Reason: Explains how desiring things other than God leaves a believer cold, barren and dry.
7. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0034): «Let us only be careless or "faint in our mind," let us be easy and indolent, and our natural darkness will soon return, and overspread our soul.» Reason: Spiritual sloth alone, without gross sin, is enough to darken the soul; a likely cause of drift.
8. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0043): «Now, when so various assaults are made at once, and perhaps with the utmost violence, it is not strange if it should occasion, not only heaviness, but even darkness in a weak believer» Reason: Shows that unexpected temptations after a calm season can plunge a believer into darkness.
9. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0048): «Whereas, indeed, the cure of spiritual, as of bodily diseases, must be as various as are the causes of them. The first thing, therefore, is to find out the cause; and this will naturally point out the cure.» Reason: Wesley's starting counsel for recovery: identify the cause of the darkness, which points to the cure.
10. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0049): «And how can you expect they should return, till you put away the accursed thing?» Reason: Direct counsel: if sin drove away joy and peace, forsake it and the Lord will return and pardon.
11. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0057): «It is vain to hope for a recovery of his light, till you pluck out the right eye, and cast it from you. O let there be no longer delay! Cry to Him, that he may enable you so to do!» Reason: How to get the light back when an idol is the cause: cry to God, cast out every idol.
12. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0059): «Arise, and shake yourself from the dust; wrestle with God for the mighty blessing; pour out your soul unto God in prayer, and continue therein with all perseverance!» Reason: Cure for a soul gone dead through spiritual sloth: stir up, pray earnestly and persevere.
13. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0060): «"Commune with him in your chamber, and be still;" and desire of him to try the ground of your heart, and bring to your remembrance whatever has at any time offended the eyes of his glory.» Reason: Counsel when no present cause is found: ask God to search past sins and renew by repentance and faith.
14. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0073): «Joy in the Holy Ghost will far more effectually purify the soul than the want of that joy; and the peace of God is the best means of refining the soul from the dross of earthly affections.» Reason: Rejects the idea that dryness is better for the soul; God's presence and joy, not absence, perfect us.
15. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0075): «When either ignorance or sin has caused darkness, one or the other may be removed, and yet the light which was obstructed thereby may not immediately return. As it is the free gift of God, he may restore it, sooner or later, as it pleases him.» Reason: Answers 'can I get it back': God restores the light, though not always immediately after the cause is removed.
16. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0078): «And God will then bear witness to his word, and bring their souls out of trouble.» Reason: Promise of restoration: God brings tempted believers out of darkness and their light shines more and more.
17. #21 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 1 (wesley-021-c0071): «This whole process, both of mourning for an absent God, and recovering the joy of his countenance, seems to be shadowed out in what our Lord spoke to his Apostles» Reason: Speaks to mourning a God who seems absent and promises the sorrow will be turned into joy.
18. #28 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 8 (wesley-028-c0009): «Even after God hath opened the eyes of our understanding, if we seek or desire anything else than God, how soon is our foolish heart darkened! Then clouds again rest upon our souls.» Reason: Explains how a once-enlightened heart darkens by seeking other things, and that clouds vanish when we seek God alone.
19. #138 On Grieving the Holy Spirit (wesley-138-c0019): «At those seasons, the blessed Spirit retired and concealed his presence from us, we were justly left to a sense of our own wretchedness and misery, till we humbled ourselves before the Lord» Reason: Grieving the Spirit brings darkness; humbling ourselves with repentance and faith brings back his peace.
