column7: #137 On the Resurrection of the Dead
column8: #137 On the Resurrection of the Dead, wesley-137-c0070 (proposed): And let us not forfeit all this happiness, for want of a little more patience. Only let us hold out to the end, and we shall receive an abundant recompence for all the trouble arid uneasiness of our passage which shall be endless rest and peace. «Let this especially, fortify us against the fear of death: It is now disarmed, and can do us no hurt. It divides us, indeed, from this body awhile; but it is only that we may receive it again more glorious.» Reason: Direct comfort against fear of death: death is disarmed and only parts us from the body until resurrection.
column9:
1. #62 The End of Christ's Coming (wesley-062-c0043): «that peace which enables us in every state therewith to be content; which delivers us from all perplexing doubts, from all tormenting fears; and in particular, from that "fear of death whereby we were all our life-time subject to bondage."» Reason: Peace with God through Christ delivers from tormenting fears, in particular the fear of death.
2. #9 The Spirit of Bondage and of Adoption. (wesley-009-c0053): «Consequently, he has no fear of death; by reason whereof he was in time past, for so many years, "subject to bondage." Rather, knowing that "if the earthly house of this tabernacle be dissolved, he hath a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens;» Reason: The child of God need not fear death, knowing a house from God awaits him; answers the fear itself.
3. #28 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 8 (wesley-028-c0067): «he will teach thee to say, "O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? Thanks be unto God, who giveth" me "the victory, through" my "Lord Jesus Christ."» Reason: Promise that God will give victory over death and take away its sting at the end.
4. #7 The Way to the Kingdom (wesley-007-c0021): «And it banishes fear all such fear as hath torment the fear of the wrath of God the fear of hell the fear of the devil and in particular the fear of death» Reason: The peace of God banishes tormenting fear, in particular the fear of death.

column8: #46 The Wilderness State, wesley-046-c0060 (proposed): If, upon the fullest and most impartial examination of yourself, you cannot discern that you at present give way either to spiritual sloth, or any other inward or outward sin, then «call to mind the time that is past. Consider your former tempers, words, and actions. Have these been right before the Lord? "Commune with him in your chamber, and be still;" and desire of him to try the ground of your heart, and bring to your remembrance whatever has at any time offended the eyes of his glory.» If the guilt of any unrepented sin remain on our soul, it cannot be but you will remain in darkness, till, having been renewed by repentance, you are again washed by faith in the "fountain opened for sin and uncleanness." Reason: Speaks to not knowing whether you did wrong: recall the past, be still before God, and ask him to search your heart.
column9:
1. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0019): «He never repenteth of what he hath given, or desires to withdraw them from us. Therefore he never deserts us, as some speak; it is we only that desert him.» Reason: God does not arbitrarily withdraw himself; explains why God can feel absent and that he has not left you.
2. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0075): «When either ignorance or sin has caused darkness, one or the other may be removed, and yet the light which was obstructed thereby may not immediately return. As it is the free gift of God, he may restore it, sooner or later, as it pleases him.» Reason: Even when the cause is dealt with, the sense of God may not return at once; explains continued quiet.
3. #46 The Wilderness State (wesley-046-c0077): «Above all, let them be instructed, when the storm is upon them, not to reason with the devil, but to pray; to pour out their souls before God, and show him of their trouble.» Reason: In spiritual darkness and temptation, keep praying and pour out your soul to God rather than arguing with doubts.
4. #138 On Grieving the Holy Spirit (wesley-138-c0019): «At those seasons, the blessed Spirit retired and concealed his presence from us, we were justly left to a sense of our own wretchedness and misery, till we humbled ourselves before the Lord, and by deep repentance and active faith obtained a return of divine mercy and peace.» Reason: Describes the Spirit seeming to withdraw his presence and how it returns through humbling and faith.
5. #77 Spiritual Worship (wesley-077-c0054): «Lo! God is here! not afar off. Now believe and feel him near!» Reason: Direct reply to feeling God is far: he is about your bed and path, not afar off.

column8: #6 The Righteousness of Faith, wesley-006-c0061 (proposed): 6. To conclude. Whosoever thou art, O man, who hast the sentence of death in thyself, who feelest thyself a condemned sinner, and hast the wrath of God abiding on thee: Unto thee saith the Lord, not, "Do this," -- perfectly obey all my commands, -- "and live;" but, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved." "The word of faith is nigh unto thee:" «Now, at this instant, in the present moment, and in thy present state, sinner as thou art, just as thou art, believe the gospel; and "I will be merciful unto thy unrighteousness, and thy iniquities will I remember no more."» Reason: Tells the one who has sinned to come to God now, just as they are, with the promise of mercy and forgiveness.
column9:
1. #8 THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE SPIRIT (wesley-008-c0057): «Art thou fallen, O man of God? yet, do not lie there, fretting thyself and bemoaning thy weakness; but meekly say, "Lord, I shall fall every moment, unless thou uphold me with thy hand." And then arise! Leap and walk!» Reason: Direct counsel to a believer who has fallen: don't lie there fretting; ask God's help and get up again.
2. #8 THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE SPIRIT (wesley-008-c0053): «Therefore, God is merciful to thee a sinner! such a sinner as thou art! God is love; and Christ hath died! column8: #25 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 5, wesley-025-c0074 (proposed): Do you neglect no opportunity of attending and partaking of the Christian sacrifice? How many are they who call themselves Christians, and yet are utterly regardless of it, -- yet do not eat of that bread, or drink of that cup, for months, perhaps years, together? Do you, every day, either hear the Scriptures, or read them and meditate thereon? «Do you join in prayer with the great congregation, daily, if you have opportunity; if not, whenever you can; particularly on that day which you "remember to keep it holy?" Do you strive to "make opportunities?" Are you glad when they say unto you, "We will go into the house of the Lord?"» Are you zealous of, and diligent in, private prayer? Reason: Presses the reluctant to join public worship whenever possible, especially on Sunday, and to be glad to go to God's house.

1. #24 Upon our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse 4 (wesley-024-c0014): «Yet such retirement must not swallow up all our time; this would be to destroy, not advance, true religion. For, that the religion described by our Lord in the foregoing words cannot subsist without society, without our living and conversing with other men» Reason: Says private, solitary religion destroys true religion; Christianity cannot subsist apart from life with other believers.
2. #48 Self-denial (wesley-048-c0053): «And why does he not continue in prayer? Because in time of dryness it is pain and grief unto him. He does not continue in hearing at all opportunities, because sleep is sweet; or it is cold, or dark, or rainy.» Reason: Diagnoses skipping worship for comfort ('sleep is sweet') as a lack of self-denial that stalls growth in grace.
